jobs.title: Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician (Overnight) - Newton, MA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As an Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician, you’re part of a team that thrives on the front lines of emergency veterinary care where every second counts. You’ll handle a wide range of cases, from minor to complex emergencies, collaborating with our doctors and team in delivering gold standard, emotionally intelligent care. You’ll jump into triage, treatments, diagnostics, anesthesia, monitoring, and critical care nursing, all while being a steady, compassionate presence for pet parents in their most stressful moments. This role is for someone who wants to do the work they were trained to do (and more), continue growing their skills, and help people and their pets when they need it most.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Treat every patient and person like they matter—because they do! You keep people and pets together and stay by their side through tests, treatments, and everything in between

• Jump into action, delivering nursing care, treatments, and emotional support in the most critical moments, from triage to discharge

• Bring the meds, the monitoring, and the mastery—from IVs and CRIs to blood transfusions and beyond

• Communicate like a teammate and think like a leader, helping shape plans and keep care flowing

• Be ready to perform CPR like the trained RECOVER rockstar you are (not only do we offer training, we have the highest number of RECOVER CPR professionals and instructors in the industry!)

• All the techy stuff—from diagnostics and imaging to sample collection and placing tubes

• Anesthesia, even for our most fragile patients? You’ve got it.

• Use all the advanced techniques in your toolkit: central lines, endoscopy, ultrasounds, and more

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate’s degree or higher in veterinary technology from an AVMA accredited program strongly preferred

• Credentialed as a Veterinary Technician (CVT, RVT, LVT, LVMT) in the state the VEG practice is located is required; VTS in ECC, internal medicine or anesthesia/analgesia is a plus and will lead to extra considerations in compensation

• 1+ years of experience in a veterinary technician role; experience in emergency or specialty medicine preferred

• Basic computer skills and a comprehension of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

• Excellent communicator and calm under pressure; ready to lend a hand to support those around you

• Fine motor skills for handling patients and medical equipment

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors.

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation ($27-68/hr), including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, GTM Talent Acquisition - North America
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.




THE ROLE

Legora recently passed $200M in ARR, doubling in less than six months. North America is our fastest-growing market, our largest, and the one where competition is fiercest. We're hiring at significant scale across the teams that sell, deploy and grow Legora, from our New York, San Francisco, Chicago, Denver, Houston, Toronto and Mexico City offices. We need someone to lead that hiring and the 10+ person team behind it.

Based in our New York office, you'll lead all GTM recruiting across North America: sales, engagement, legal engineering and marketing. You'll report to our new Senior Director of Global GTM Talent Acquisition and be accountable for the quality, pace and consistency of GTM hiring across the US, Canada and Mexico. The scope will grow as the team scales.

You'll work with our CRO, sales and Marketing leadership team on how we build the GTM organization, including workforce planning, org design and the hiring strategy behind each new team and market. Our leaders are invested in recruiting, they make time for it, and they expect it to move as fast as the business.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and develop a team of Talent Partners across sales, engagement, legal engineering and marketing. Hire and grow the team as demand scales, with a core in New York close to the business and talent partners across our other North American hubs.

 - Run the operation tightly. You're in the detail on hiring plans, pipeline health, interview process and team capacity, and you drive the changes needed to make them work at scale.

 - Own the relationships with North American leaders in sales, engagement, legal engineering and marketing as a genuine hiring partner. Contribute to role scoping, success profiles and hiring strategy rather than waiting to be handed a brief.

 - Move easily between the detail and the exec room. Give executives a clear, honest picture of where every search stands, and handle escalations with the credibility to hold your ground.

 - Build pipelines ahead of demand across every function and hub. Much of the talent we need is passive, so you'll get the business behind hiring through outreach from hiring managers, referrals, and persistence across channels.

 - Hold the standard for candidate experience across your team, from first conversation through to offer. Every interaction should reflect the quality of the product and the people behind it.

 - Partner with the Senior Director of Global GTM Talent Acquisition and your European counterpart on process consistency and shared standards as both regions scale.




WHAT YOU BRING

You've led recruiting teams across multiple GTM functions at companies with a world-class hiring bar and a plan that kept changing. You've seen more than one GTM organization up close, so you know what works, what doesn't, and how to bring consistency and rigor to hiring across very different profiles, from quota-carrying sellers to former lawyers and marketers. You have some battle scars, and you're at a point in your career where you want to be all in.

We're looking for:

 - Several years managing recruiting teams of real size. This isn't your first leadership role. You've hired and developed recruiters, kept a team motivated through a demanding stretch, and been accountable for outcomes rather than activity.

 - Time inside best-in-class GTM hiring functions, at high-growth, VC-backed or top-tier companies where the bar was genuinely high.

 - Breadth across GTM hiring. You've led or closely overseen hiring for sales plus at least one of customer success or engagement, marketing, or specialist or technical roles. Experience recruiting lawyers or legal professionals is a strong plus.

 - A mix of agency and in-house experience preferred. You've seen recruiting from both sides and built resilience from it.

 - The depth to hold credible conversations with senior leaders, up to CRO level, about what strong looks like at each level. You know the difference between a good resume and a good hire, and you don't lower the bar when searches get difficult.

 - Experience leading teams across multiple sites.

 - An operator's approach to running searches. You track the right things, use pipeline data to make decisions, and change the process when it isn't working.

 - A hiring bar that doesn't move under pressure. When searches get hard, you change the approach, not the standard.




WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America.

 - Competitive package: Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success.

 - Meaningful work: Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily.

 - In-person environment: Union Square office designed for ambitious builders and company provided lunch daily.

 - Benefits & Perks: We invest in our people with a comprehensive, thoughtfully designed benefits package:
   Medical, Dental & Vision
   
   - Multiple medical plan options through Aetna and Kaiser Permanente
   
   - HSA or Healthcare FSA (based on plan selection)
   
   - Dental plans via MetLife
   
   - Vision plans via Vision Care
   
   Family Support
   
   - Generous parental leave
   
   - Free access to Maven Clinic
   
   - Dependent Care FSA
   
   - Free One Medical membership for employees and dependents
   
   Additional Perks
   
   - Pre-tax commuter benefits
   
   - Life Insurance + STD/LTD
   
   - 401(K) with generous company match
   
   - Unlimited PTO
   
   - Robust voluntary benefits, including identity protection (via Aura), legal coverage via MetLife, pet savings programs, and more

Legora is an Equal Opportunity Employer

At Legora, we believe great teams are built on diversity of thought and experience. We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. We welcome people of all backgrounds and don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Market Clinician Lead
jobs.description:
Market Clinician Lead

Location: Jacksonville, FL Market (On-site)
Reports to: Chief Medical Officer
Partners with: Operations Market Leader
Role Type: Full-time, Exempt (Blended Clinical & Leadership)

About Bluebird Kids Health

Bluebird Kids Health provides value-based pediatric primary care to underserved communities with a mission to help every child thrive. Our care model combines comprehensive primary and urgent care with care coordination, chronic disease management, and population health programs to improve outcomes, enhance the patient and family experience, and lower the total cost of care.

Position Summary

The Market Clinician Lead is the senior clinical leader for a defined market and one half of the market leadership dyad. Partnering with the Market Leader (Operations), you are responsible for clinical quality, patient safety, provider development, and consistent execution of Bluebird's pediatric care model. Together, the dyad is accountable for market performance across growth, quality, patient experience, employee engagement, and operational excellence.

This is a practicing physician role with protected administrative time. You will maintain a patient panel while providing clinical leadership across the market.

This is a highly visible, boots-on-the-ground leadership role. Success comes from being present in our practices—observing care delivery, coaching providers in real time, mentoring teams, removing barriers to excellent care, and identifying opportunities for improvement through direct engagement with patients, providers, and staff. Administrative leadership is expected to occur primarily within the practices you support, not from a remote office.

Key Responsibilities

• Frontline Clinical Leadership: Maintain a strong presence across market practices, building trusted relationships with providers and staff. Observe care delivery firsthand, provide real-time coaching, identify opportunities for improvement, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning. Lead implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of Bluebird's pediatric care model across all market locations, ensuring consistent, high-quality care.

• Quality & Safety: Drive clinical quality, patient safety, and population health outcomes, including well-child visits, immunizations, lead screening, chronic disease management, and clinical safety event review and resolution.

• Evidence-Based Care: Partner with the Chief Medical Officer and clinician leadership to develop, implement, and reinforce evidence-based clinical guidelines, standardized care pathways, and best practices.

• Provider Development: Recruit, onboard, mentor, coach, and retain providers. Lead peer review, support performance management, and create an environment of continuous professional development and clinical excellence.

• Value-Based Performance: Drive the clinical levers that improve total cost of care, including appropriate referral management, medication stewardship, documentation and coding quality, chronic disease management, and reduction of avoidable emergency department utilization.

• Operational Partnership: Partner with the Market Leader to align clinical excellence with operational performance. Participate in market leadership meetings, maintain a visible presence across practice locations, and support operational initiatives that improve patient access, efficiency, and the care experience.

• Community Relationships: Develop and strengthen relationships with pediatric specialists, hospitals, and community partners to improve care coordination and ensure seamless transitions of care for patients and families.

• Organizational Agility and Growth: Embrace evolving responsibilities and contribute to emerging priorities as the organization grows, continuously improves, and adapts to meet the needs of the communities we serve.

Qualifications

• MD or DO with board certification in Pediatrics (Family Medicine considered with predominantly pediatric experience).

• Active, unrestricted medical license and DEA registration (or eligibility before start).

• Five or more years of pediatric primary care experience.

• Two or more years of physician leadership experience preferred.

• Experience in value-based care, population health, HEDIS, quality metrics, and provider performance improvement preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to develop clinicians, interpret performance data, and lead measurable improvement.

• Strong EHR, documentation, and coding proficiency.

• Ability to travel regularly between market practice locations.

• Spanish or Haitian Creole proficiency is a plus.

Who You Are

• You are a visible, approachable physician leader who enjoys leading from the clinic rather than the office.

• You build trust through presence, collaboration, and mentorship.

• You are passionate about improving pediatric care by coaching colleagues, developing teams, and solving problems where care is delivered.

• You are comfortable using data to identify opportunities and working alongside providers and staff to implement practical solutions.

• You believe exceptional patient outcomes are achieved through consistent execution, accountability, and strong relationships.

What We Offer

• Opportunity to lead clinical care in a growing value-based pediatric organization.

• Competitive compensation package with performance incentives.

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits.

• Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts.

• Disability, employee assistance, caregiver support, commuter, and wellness benefits.

• Generous paid time off.

• A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant opportunities for professional growth.

jobs.title: Workforce Management Analyst
jobs.description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

About the Role

IQ Grow pairs every restaurant on the bundle with a Marketing Success Manager (MSM) — a dedicated human to drive sales to the restaurant. Demand has outpaced our plan, and the program now scales on the back of a fast, continuous hiring cadence. Every new MSM has to be hired, provisioned, onboarded, assigned a book of restaurants, and tracked.

This role owns that machine. You'll be the operational backbone of the MSM workforce: making sure every new hire lands with the right system access on day one, that restaurants are matched to the right MSM, and that we have a single reliable source of truth for who is in the program, what they're working on, and where the gaps are. It's an entry-level role with unusual visibility

A day in the life (Responsibilities)

• Own new-hire readiness and systems access: Drive every MSM from offer to fully operational. Submit and track access requests across Zip, Salesforce, Toast internal tools, and the marketing agent; confirm provisioning is complete before the start date; and chase the exceptions so no MSM sits idle in their first week. Build the checklist that makes this repeatable, then push to automate it.

• Facilitate the hiring cadence: Partner with recruiting and the contracting team to keep requisitions, offers, paperwork, and start dates moving on schedule. Maintain the hiring tracker, flag slips against plan, and group start dates into cohorts so onboarding and training happen in batches rather than one-offs.

• Manage MSM-to-restaurant assignment: Run the process that matches new and existing restaurants to MSMs — balancing book size, segment or cuisine fit, time zone, and MSM tenure. Keep assignments current through churn, reassignment, and MSM departures, and make sure every restaurant has a named owner at all times.

• Close the loop on program health: Track onboarding and offboarding completion, surface recurring friction (access delays, unassigned restaurants, MSMs over or under capacity), and propose fixes. Coordinate offboarding and access removal cleanly when contracts end.

• Support capacity planning: Feed clean roster, attrition, and book-size data into the team's capacity model, and help translate restaurant growth into an MSM hiring need. You won't own the model, but you'll own the inputs that make it credible.

What You'll Work With

• A small, fast-moving team

• Cross-functional partners across recruiting, enablement, IT and access management, finance, and MSM management

• A distributed workforce of marketing success managers across multiple geographies and time zones

• Tooling that's early by design: expect to build the tracker before you get the platform

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

• 0–2 years in operations, program or workforce coordination, recruiting coordination, HR ops, or a similarly process-heavy role

• Exceptional follow-through: you keep a long list of small, unglamorous things moving without being asked twice

• Strong spreadsheet and tracker skills, and the instinct to notice when a manual process should become a system

• Clear written communication across many stakeholders, including people more senior than you

• Comfort with ambiguity

• Bonus: exposure to access and provisioning workflows or workforce management concepts

AI at Toast

At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it’s a core part of our culture.

Our Total Rewards Philosophy
We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters’ changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits.

The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. You can learn more about how we align pay with local labor markets in our Geographic Pay Zone Philosophy.

Zone A

$58,000—$93,000 USD

Zone B

$50,000—$80,000 USD

Zone C

$45,000—$72,000 USD

How Toast Uses AI in its Hiring Process

Throughout the hiring process, our goal is to get to know you. We use AI tools to support our recruiters and interviewers with tasks like note-taking, summarization, and documentation of interviews to ensure they can be fully focused on your conversation. All hiring decisions are made by people. We ask that you complete interviews and assessments on your own, without real-time AI tools, recording, or transcription bots, unless we tell you otherwise in advance. To learn more: https://careers.toasttab.com/ai-in-hiring

Our Approach to Hybrid Working

We embrace a hybrid work model that fosters in-person collaboration while valuing individual needs. Our goal is to build a strong culture of connection as we work together to empower the hospitality community, regardless of location. Please visit the Locations page on our career site to learn more about our in-office expectations by region: https://careers.toasttab.com/locations-toast

People Are the Secret Ingredient in Our Recipe for Success

At Toast, our employees are our secret ingredient—when they thrive, we thrive. The restaurant industry brings together people with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we value that same breadth at Toast. We strive to build a culture grounded in authenticity, respect, and humility, where every Toaster has a real opportunity to grow, contribute, and do their best work—raising the bar in delivering exceptional experiences for our customers and each other.

Apply today!

As part of this commitment, we strive to provide reasonable accommodations for persons with disabilities to enable them to access the hiring process. jobs.description:

Our Guiding Principles:

Position Summary:

This role partners closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and executive leadership to ensure the organization’s fiscal health and alignment with its mission and long-term objectives. The CFO is responsible for budget planning and forecasting, financial compliance, strategic financial planning, and optimizing systems and resources to support business growth. The CFO also oversees large-scale capital projects and works to enhance organizational sustainability through sound financial stewardship.

Compensation & Benefits:

Job Duties & Functions:

• Lead the organization’s budget development, oversight, and management, including cash flow, investments, and banking relationships.

• Supervise the Controller and other accounting staff to ensure timely and accurate budget preparation, financial reporting, and compliance.

• Maintain and enhance fiscal control systems and policies in alignment with GAAP and nonprofit regulatory standards.

• Present annual budgets and monthly financial updates to the Finance Committee of the Board of Directors.

• CPA credential or equivalent certification required.

jobs.title: Buyer, Construction Subcontracts, Data Center Projects
jobs.description:
About Giga

Giga is building gigawatts of AI data centers to hasten a future of intelligence and abundance. We build data centers fast and at scale by combining the capabilities of an equipment supplier, engineering firm, general contractor, and real estate developer under one roof. Our team moves quickly and thinks practically. If you're ready to make an impact in an industry that matters, we're looking for people like you.

Why join Giga

• The Pace: We're building at a speed most companies talk about but never actually operate at. If you've been bored somewhere else, you won't be here.

• The Impact: Every person at Giga touches the work that matters. No layers, no waiting for approval chains. You'll see your fingerprints on what we ship.

• The Team: A team of operators defining the future of AI infrastructure. We recruit A-players from the most innovative companies in the world, and they choose Giga because the work here means more.

• The Moment: AI doesn't run without power, and that's us. Giga is the picks and shovels behind the AI revolution. This industry is about to explode, and you'll be in the room where it's already happening.

What you'll do

As a Buyer, you will own subcontract packages for Giga data center projects from request to award. Reporting to the Procurement Manager, you will issue requests for proposal, level the bids, recommend the award, prepare the work order and manage the vendor through the job. You will work directly with subcontractors, and partner with Engineering and Construction to make scopes complete before they go out to bid. Legal owns the legal terms. You own the commercial outcome: scope, price, schedule and payment milestones.

Our procurement platform is AI-native. AI agents built on Claude and our Google Sheets and Drive data spine draft, log, compare and check. You will spend your time with vendors and project teams, and you will use the tools to move faster.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for a buyer who can run several live packages at once on more than one project.

Where you'll work

This role is remote. We prefer candidates based in Texas and will consider candidates anywhere in the US. Expect about 20% travel to project sites and team onsites.

Responsibilities

Sourcing and Bidding

• Own subcontract packages from request to award: civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, fire protection and specialty trades.

• Build each request for proposal with Engineering and Construction, and check the scope, drawings and specifications for gaps before issue.

• Build the bidder list, issue the package, run the pre-bid meeting and manage bidder questions and addenda through one bids mailbox.

• Level bids on a common basis and write the award recommendation: price, schedule, qualifications and risk.

• Follow the competitive bidding and approval policy. Aim for three qualified bidders on each package.

Award and Work Orders

• Prepare the work order for each award from our standard form under the master services agreement.

• Negotiate commercial terms with the vendor: scope, price, schedule and payment milestones.

• Prepare the package for Legal review and signature, and track it to execution.

• Hand each executed award to the Procurement Analyst for budget coding and schedule of values set-up.

• Evaluate vendor change order requests for scope and price with Construction and Project Controls.

Vendor Management

• Build a qualified vendor pool for each commodity and region, ahead of each new project.

• Qualify vendors: NDA, master services agreement, insurance, bonding and safety.

• Run the post-award kickoff with each vendor, and track performance through the job.

• Keep vendor records current in our vendor database.

Scale With the Business

• Stand up subcontract procurement for new sites as Giga adds projects.

• Improve our templates, playbooks and tools as the portfolio grows.

Requirements

• 3 or more years of construction procurement or subcontract buying, running competitive bids for trade packages from request for proposal to award.

• Ability to read drawings, specifications and scopes of work, and to find gaps or conflicts before award.

• Experience leveling bids and writing award recommendations.

• Working knowledge of subcontracts, work orders, change orders, certificates of insurance, bonds and retention.

• Strong vendor relationships and a habit of following up without being asked.

• Bias to action. You keep packages moving on an aggressive schedule.

Bonus points

• Owner-side construction procurement on large capital programs, such as gigafactories, data center campuses, semiconductor fabs or energy projects.

• Experience with data center, substation, MEP or mission-critical construction.

• A Texas and Oklahoma subcontractor network.

• Hands-on use of AI tools in your daily work.

• Experience with NetSuite or another ERP, and with Autodesk Construction Cloud.

How We Work

We value people who take ownership, raise risks early, communicate directly, and follow through. Incomplete information is part of the job. Make the best decision you can, document it, and adjust as the facts change. Move quickly on reversible decisions and take more care when security, safety, financial, employee, or customer risk is involved.

Benefits

• Subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance

• Equity (options) in a rapidly growing startup

• 401(k) with 4% employer match

• Unlimited PTO

• Parental leave

• Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) or Health Savings Account (HSA)

• Commuter benefits, where applicable

• Opportunities to collaborate in person at periodic team and company on-sites

Giga Energy is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Giga Energy complies with all applicable labor laws, including the California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) and other relevant state and federal regulations. jobs.title: Lead Infant/ Toddler Teacher
jobs.description:
Shape a child’s very first learning experiences. At Guidepost Montessori, our Lead Infant Guides create calm, nurturing environments where infants are respected as capable individuals from the very beginning.

If you’re passionate about early development and want to lead a thoughtfully designed classroom that supports independence, movement, and discovery, we’d love to meet you.

As a Lead Infant Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age infant classroom (ages 0–3) in a Montessori environment intentionally designed to support each child’s natural development.

In Montessori, the environment and the guide work together to nurture independence, curiosity, and confidence. You’ll thoughtfully prepare the classroom, observe each child closely, and provide individualized care that honors their unique rhythms and needs.

Most importantly, you’ll help infants develop trust in themselves and the world around them laying the foundation for lifelong learning.

What You’ll Do

• Observe each child to understand and support their physical, emotional, and cognitive development

• Respect and follow each child’s natural rhythms for sleeping, eating, and toileting

• Prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly environment that fosters trust, movement, and exploration

• Support independence by encouraging children to participate in care activities

• Build warm, meaningful relationships with children and families

• Partner closely with parents to support each child’s growth and development

• Lead and collaborate with classroom team members to create a strong, respectful community

The Montessori Prepared Environment

Every Guidepost infant classroom is fully equipped with high-quality Montessori materials and thoughtfully designed to support movement, exploration, and independence.

Our infant environments include:

• Open floor space for movement and exploration

• Child-sized furniture and materials

• Curriculum that supports independence in feeding, dressing, and toileting

• Scientifically designed materials for fine and gross motor development

• Natural elements like real plants, cozy rugs, and abundant natural light

• Beautiful, breakable materials made from wood and metal rather than plastic

• Opportunities for climbing, crawling, and discovery without restrictive devices

What We’re Looking For

• Interest in pursuing fully sponsored Montessori certification through our Prepared Montessorian Institute, or prior Montessori diploma

• Experience working with children ages 0–3 in a group care setting

• Alignment with child-led educational philosophies (Montessori, Reggio Emilia, or similar)

• Required ECE or Child Development credits

jobs.title: Graduate Software Engineer, Open Source and Linux, Canonical Ubuntu
jobs.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

We are hiring 2025 and 2026 Graduate Software Engineers into engineering teams around the world. As a global platform company we offer a wide range of software engineering challenges, in both open source products and commercial business systems. We have teams that work in a variety of languages, typically Python, Golang, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript and of course... Bash. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on tiny devices like the Raspberry Pi and new RISC-V boards, all the way up to supercomputers, clouds and Kubernetes clusters. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.

If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical. We will work with you to identify teams and projects that would be interesting and a good fit for your skills and motivations. The process is highly competitive, it will require effort and excellence to succeed if you apply here.

Most of our engineering teams work from home. We try to align a single team in a single time zone - EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia Pacific and Indian Ocean), and AMER (North, South and Central Americas). Even though you work from home, we try to ensure you always have colleagues alongside to coach and mentor you, and for the companionship of shared problem solving and pair programming. Larger projects have multiple teams and might span the globe. We work with the open source community and specialize in building teams that work well in the 'fishbowl' of open source engineering. This is full time work, five days a week, often solving hard problems with significant responsibility. We don't generally work weekends and nights and we do enjoy good holidays but we also expect productive and intense engagement Monday to Friday.

We bring all our engineering teams together in person twice a year for a deep 'sprint' with other teams to stimulate discussion and enable a wide range of career development paths. This is a fantastic way to demonstrate and develop your skill in software, learn about a wide range of technologies, make a meaningful impact to open source, and see some very interesting new cities that you might never otherwise get to visit.

If you find the open source stack amazing, and you have been a consistent high-performing student in your school and university, then this will be a challenging and exciting start to your career.

Location: This is a Globally remote role.

The role entails

• Shaping the roadmap for your product at global sprints every six months

• Focusing on design and user experience, even for developer tooling and command line apps

• Writing high quality, resilient and performant code, potentially serving millions of demanding daily users

• Working towards mastery of key programming languages and Linux system knowledge

• Engaging with users and the open source community through code reviews and issue trackers

• Responding to customer issues as a priority, develop an understanding of enterprise requirements

• Developing skills and awareness of security in software design and implementation

What we are looking for in you

• Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university

• Undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Business Informatics, Mathematics or another STEM discipline with programming courses

• Confidence to get started and deliver high quality code in one of Python, Rust, C/C++, Golang, JavaScript or Java

• Experience with Ubuntu or another Linux distribution

• Track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results

• Result-oriented and organized, with the drive to meet commitments

• Personal projects in technology and software engineering beyond the curriculum

• Professional written and spoken English

• Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability

• Personal responsibility and accountability

• Thoughtfulness, self-awareness and the ability to reflect and develop

• Ability to travel internationally twice a year for company events up to two weeks long

Nice-to-have skills

• Upstream open source contributions

• Packaging and Linux distribution contributions - Debian, Fedora, Arch, Nix or another

• Leadership and organization skills

• Presentation and writing skills

• Business and commercial interests

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

• Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person

• Annual compensation review

• Recognition rewards

• Annual holiday leave

• Maternity and paternity leave

• Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform

• Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues

• Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

jobs.title: Permit Reviewer - Flexible Hours
jobs.description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We are recruiting US-based architects and certified plans examiners to evaluate the output of an AI system that performs automated building-code compliance review on architectural permit applications.

The system ingests permit submissions — new builds, alterations, modifications — and issues a compliant or non-compliant determination for each applicable check, drawn from the International Building Code. Every determination comes with a cited code provision and a marked location on the drawing set showing the evidence relied upon.

Your job is to tell us where the system got it wrong. You are applying the same judgment you already apply in plan review or permit preparation, to a set of determinations that have already been made. Where the system is correct, you confirm it. Where it is wrong, you correct it and the correction becomes training signal.

This is expert review work, not data entry. There is no volume of repetitive clicking to grind through and no generalist labeling pool to compete with — the entire premise of the program is that these judgments cannot be made by anyone without real code expertise.

What You’ll Own:

• Review and correct pass/fail verdicts, written rationales, and citation boxes on PDF plans using the in-tool editing toolkit.

• QA and correct labeling: Review AI-generated outputs, fix mislabeled data, and grade agent performance against what a real permit reviewer would conclude.

• Interpret permitting checklists as an experienced reviewer would, applying the relevant requirements to the submitted plans.

• Trace checklist requirements to their applicable source: IBC, IRC or other model codes, state building codes, or county/jurisdiction-specific amendments. Explain which requirement applies and why.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• ICC certification relevant to building plan review, plus actual experience reviewing permit applications and issuing or resolving plan review comments.

• Based in the United States, with at least 2 years of hands-on permitting experience; 5+ years strongly preferred.

• Deep knowledge of how permitting actually works in the United States, with a preference for experience in Arizona, California, Florida, or Texas.

• Plan examiner or Certified Building Official (CBO) experience and credentials. Provide certification details and the jurisdictions and project types you have reviewed.

The expected hourly range for this position is $50-$75 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Please be aware of recruitment scams involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent employers. Innodata will never ask for payment, banking details, or sensitive personal information during the application process. To learn more on how to recognize job scams, please visit the Federal Trade Commission’s guide at https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a recruitment scam, please report it to Innodata at verifyjoboffer@innodata.com and consider reporting it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

jobs.title: Head of People
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

Launch Potato is about 200 people, profitable, and growing. The performance management system that got us here was built by our SVP of Talent, and he still runs it. That system becomes yours.

You're inheriting something that works. There's a levels framework, a rating scale, a calibration process, and managers who have been through several cycles. It got us to 200 people. Your job is deciding what carries forward and change-managing the rest, across an org that moves fast and adopts new processes.

We want someone who'll find the version that works and then hold it there while the company gets good at it.

If you want to own a function, make it extraordinary, and be judged on whether it actually got better, keep reading.

Why This Seat

• Real ownership, immediately. Performance, total rewards, and compliance are yours to own rather than support. You'll defend a compensation number in front of a CFO who checks it.

• An SVP who wants to hand this over. Not one who says that and then rewrites your deck. The explicit goal is that the HR function runs without him.

• Executive reach by default. Calibration and leveling decisions live with the C-suite, and you present your own work. You won't spend year one convincing anyone that performance management matters.

• Leverage is part of the mandate, not a side project. We are tech-first and AI-forward, which means we can run lean teams and do more with less. You'll push that further, build the tooling managers actually open, and make everything easier without taking substance out of it. Nobody will ask you to do it the slow way.

How This Team Is Led

From Kris Osborne, SVP of Talent.

I'll tell you what I want and what the constraints are and then get out of the way. I don't rewrite people's work. If I disagree with where you landed you'll hear it from me early, and if you still think you're right then push back, because I'd rather change my mind than have you go quiet and build something you don't believe in.

I ask before I decide. When something changes the shape of this team the people on it hear it from me first and they get a real say in it, not a heads up after it's done.

I care about the outcome and I'm not going to do your job for you. Bring me a problem and I'll work it with you, but I'm not going to take it off your plate and hand it back finished.

I'm hiring this seat because I want someone we can all learn from. Bring me a better answer than mine and I'll take it.

What You'll Bring

Six things, all six required.

• A full performance cycle you owned end to end, not supported. Owned more than once, at 150 people or more. Design, timeline, manager prep, calibration, rollout, retro.

• Compensation and benefits you've owned. Band design, benchmarking methodology, benefits renewals, the annual comp cycle. You can defend a number to a CFO.

• HR compliance as standing scope, not as a project. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. You've inherited a backlog and cleared it.

• A people system that outlasted you. Built, adopted, and still recognizable two cycles later.

• Leverage you built that people adopted. You've automated or rebuilt part of a people process so it ran faster, the quality held or improved, and the team actually used it. Adoption is the test here, the same way durability is the test above.

• Experience taking a company our size to materially larger, on headcount or revenue, more than once. You know what breaks first at the next stage because you've watched it break.

• Empowered your team to raise the bar. You have clear examples of coaching, mentoring, and growing a team that created extraordinary outcomes.

This is a player-coach seat. Managers here lead a team and deliver work personally, at every level.

Nice to Have

• You have opinions about what performance management gets wrong, and specific examples of what you changed

• You can tell a process problem from a manager-capability problem, and you fix the right one

• You're the person who says the uncomfortable thing in a calibration room

What You'll Own

Performance management. The mid-year and annual cycles end to end: design, timeline, communication, execution. What the cycle needs to produce and what to cut. A timeline published early enough that managers plan around it. The retro after each one, and the judgment about when a change is warranted and when to leave it alone.

Total rewards. Band design and the benchmarking methodology behind it. Benefits renewals and the economics underneath them. The annual comp cycle, with leveling and pay kept connected.

Compliance. Multi-state registration, I-9, handbook, classification, postings. The current backlog, plus the escalation and coverage protocols that follow it.

Manager enablement. Preparing managers for real performance conversations, including the one where someone rated themselves higher than their manager did. The calibration process, including where two managers apply the same bar differently. Playbooks and self-service resources so a manager gets an answer without booking a meeting. Standing support for the roughly three dozen front-line managers who get it reactively today.

Leverage and tooling. Finding the parts of everything above that shouldn't be done by hand, and fixing them. Building what a manager will actually open rather than what looks good in a demo. Taking time out of the cycle while the conversations get better rather than thinner.

The team. An HR Business Partner and a Total Rewards and People Analytics lead. Both are strong at what they do and both have room to grow. You set their decision rights: where they decide, where they recommend, where it comes to you.

What Great Looks Like

In your first year:

• The annual cycle ships on your timeline and you own it

• Managers are calibrated before the cycle rather than corrected after it

• Every person leaving a check-in has one clear thing to work on, and the conversation that produced it was a real one

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Infrastructure Programs
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Vultr is on a mission to make high-performance cloud infrastructure easy to use, affordable, and locally accessible for enterprises and AI innovators around the world. With 33 global cloud data center locations, Vultr is trusted by hundreds of thousands of active customers across 185 countries for its flexible, scalable, global Cloud Compute, Cloud GPU, Bare Metal, and Cloud Storage solutions. In December 2024 Vultr announced an equity financing at a $3.5 billion valuation. Founded by David Aninowsky and self-funded for over a decade, Vultr has grown to become the world’s largest privately-held cloud infrastructure company.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the end-to-end digital turn-up, onboarding, and validation of our data center infrastructure.

In this role, you will take ownership on driving the logical orchestration required to bring our most complex, large-scale AI data center builds online for production use.

Acting as the critical link between site delivery, core engineering, and platform teams, you will coordinate network setup, storage and compute infrastructure, GPU cluster onboarding, system stress testing, and operational handoffs. Your leadership will ensure our next-generation, high-performance infrastructure is delivered on time, highly stable, and fully optimized.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Program Execution

 - Drive end-to-end execution from hardware power-on to production readiness, managing timelines across automated provisioning, compute, storage, and networking setups.

2. Cross-Functional Orchestration

 - Lead syncs across Network, Compute, Storage, GPU, Platform, and Infra Ops teams to unblock technical issues and align delivery schedules.

 - Serve as the single point of contact for tracking critical path dependencies and managing engineering risks.

3. Solution Productization

 - Partner with engineering to scope, test, and deploy custom, client-requested infrastructure architectures.

 - Help convert unique client requirements into repeatable, standardized product offerings and automated delivery frameworks.

4. Customer & Stakeholder Alignment

 - Interface directly with strategic customer technical teams as the main point of contact for Engineering requirements.

 - Work with Infrastructure Operations, Solutions, Product, and Customer Success to align technical delivery with business commitments.


QUALIFICATIONS

Technical Depth & Program Leadership

 - Technical Program Management: 10+ years leading large-scale infrastructure deployments, cloud/data center turn-ups, or technical program lifecycles.

 - GPU & AI Infrastructure: Technical familiarity with AI accelerators (e.g., NVIDIA, AMD), high-speed GPU interconnects, and cluster topologies.

 - Networking, Compute & Storage: Strong knowledge of data center networks (BGP, leaf-spine), Linux systems, and distributed storage.

 - Execution & Rigor: Proven track record managing complex dependencies, implementing validation testing, and meeting strict deadlines.

Strategy, Business & Communication

 - Ambiguity Navigation: Ability to create structure out of uncertainty, identify bottlenecks early, and drive solutions.

 - Communication & Influence: Strong written and verbal skills, with a proven ability to align cross-functional teams and leadership.

 - Data-Driven Problem Solving: Analytical mindset using metrics to track program health and make decisions.

Education & Certifications

 - Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; MBA or master's degree is a plus.

 - Certifications: PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification preferred, but not required.


INCLUSION & PRIVACY

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and we prohibit discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable laws. Vultr will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with applicable laws and will not conduct a background check until after an offer of employment has been extended and accepted.

We also take your privacy seriously. We handle personal information responsibly and follow applicable laws, including U.S. privacy rules and India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Your data is used only for legitimate business purposes and is protected with proper security measures.

Where allowed by law, applicants may request details about the data we collect, access or delete their information, withdraw consent for its use, and opt out of nonessential communications. For more details, please see our Privacy Policy https://www.vultr.com/legal/privacy/.

jobs.title: Culture Editor
jobs.location: Miami, FL or New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Us

Dorsia is at the forefront of hospitality-tech innovation, redefining how the world gains access to the most in-demand restaurants, events, and experiences. By fusing cutting-edge technology with the art of luxury hospitality, we empower our members to secure impossible-to-get reservations while providing operators with unprecedented levels of control, visibility, and revenue optimization.

In 2025, we grew revenue 480% and scaled to 400+ venues across 25 destinations, with the launch of our Culture Calendar extending Dorsia beyond restaurants into the world's most sought-after cultural moments.

Backed by $54M in funding from investors including Index Ventures, Invus, and Red Sea Ventures, and strategic partners including MoonPay, Major Food Group, and The Dinex Group / Daniel Boulud, we are entering our most consequential phase of growth and reshaping the global hospitality landscape. We're adding exceptional talent to drive what comes next.

About the Role

Dorsia is seeking a Culture Editor to own our Culture Calendar, a dedicated section of the Dorsia app combining a curated global guide to events in art, fashion, design, architecture, and music with original interviews and features. You’ll identify the events worth our members’ attention, keep listings accurate and current, and develop original coverage for the app, social,  and our monthly Culture Edit newsletter.

You bring strong editorial judgment, a distinct voice, and an established network of artists, designers, musicians, luxury sports figures, and cultural insiders. You’re a versatile writer who can deliver sharp copy, substantive interviews, concise cultural recommendations, party reports, and neighborhood guides with local insight. You know how to find a story, ask informed questions, and move beyond an announcement to explain why something matters. You’re equally comfortable conducting engaging interviews and commissioning a creative to make an exclusive playlist for Dorsia’s Spotify. You know what good looks like.

Dorsia embraces AI and automation across the business. You’ll use these tools throughout your workflow: supporting research, interview preparation, transcription, brainstorming, editing, organization, and repeatable calendar operations. Original editorial will be grounded in your reporting, writing, access, and point of view. You’ll also work closely with product and engineering to improve the systems behind the Culture Calendar.

What You’ll Do

Editorial and Content

• Pitch, report, and write original interviews, features, and cultural coverage for Dorsia’s app, social, and monthly Culture Edit newsletter, including select collaborations with Surface magazine.

• Develop timely story ideas through cultural knowledge, relationships, and firsthand reporting, and evaluate incoming editorial opportunities.

• Secure and conduct interviews that produce fresh insights, specific details, and original material.

• Evaluate incoming editorial opportunities and pursue the people and stories worth covering.

• Work with editorial leadership to plan coverage, shape stories, and deliver accurate, publication-ready copy on deadline.

Culture Calendar

• Own the Culture Calendar’s editorial selection, listings, and ongoing maintenance in Nucleus, Dorsia’s content management system.

• Track major cultural moments and the exhibitions, openings, performances, and ancillary programming around them, extending coverage beyond Dorsia’s own events.

• Balance established institutions and tentpole events with emerging voices and discoveries that deserve members’ attention.

• Research and verify dates, locations, access details, and other essential information, keeping listings current as programming changes.

• Write and edit concise listings that explain what an event is and why it matters.

• Set coverage priorities across Dorsia’s markets.

AI and Workflow Development

• Use AI as a research, brainstorming, and editing partner, and for interview preparation, transcription, and organizing source material.

• Adopt, configure, and improve AI tools and automated workflows for announcement monitoring, event-detail extraction, tagging, and routine listing preparation.

• Apply editorial judgment and verification throughout these workflows, taking responsibility for the accuracy and quality of published content.

• Maintain shared style guidance, source records, and institutional knowledge that make the team’s work more consistent and efficient.

• Stay curious about new tools and identify practical ways to improve research, production, and calendar maintenance.

Relationships and In-Market Presence

• Build and maintain relationships with creatives, cultural institutions, publications, and press contacts internationally to secure contributors, surface stories, and identify programming.

• Attend openings, fairs, fashion weeks, and festivals, bringing firsthand observations and discoveries into Dorsia’s coverage.

• Travel periodically for reporting and relationship building during key cultural moments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner with product and engineering as a calendar power user, testing functionality, reporting bugs, and recommending improvements to editorial workflows and the member experience.

• Support business development by identifying relevant cultural programming and partnership opportunities.

• Work with brand and marketing to adapt editorial coverage across Dorsia’s channels, using automation where it improves production and distribution.

• Maintain a disciplined editorial schedule and project management system in Notion, keeping events, deadlines, and deliverables on track.

The Winning Recipe

• Bachelor's degree in Journalism, English, Art History, Communications, or a related field.

• 3-5 years of editorial experience in culture publishing, luxury media, new media, or a brand editorial team, with the ability to work independently.

• A portfolio of published cultural reporting that demonstrates original interviews, strong writing, editorial judgment, and a distinct voice.

• Regular, hands-on use of AI and automation in editorial work, with examples of how you’ve applied these tools to improve your work

• An established network that helps you secure interviews and contributors, discover stories, and understand cultural scenes in multiple international cities.

• Deep knowledge of one or more of our core disciplines across art, fashion, design, architecture, and music, with a curiosity across the others.

• The ability to distinguish a compelling story from a promotional announcement and explain its relevance to Dorsia’s members.

• Experience managing an events calendar, listings database, or content catalog with accuracy and attention to detail.

• Fluency in Notion and comfort working in a content management system, including testing features and communicating issues to product and engineering.

• Strong project management skills and clear, confident communication with creatives, partners, and colleagues.

• An active presence in cultural communities and willingness to travel periodically for reporting and key events.

Compensation:

New York Pay Range

$80,000—$95,000 USD

Workplace Philosophy at Dorsia

At Dorsia, we believe that culture eats strategy. The best ideas in the world mean nothing without the right people around the table and the right chemistry between them. We are, unapologetically, a people-first organization.

In-Person Matters

We’re creating once-in-a-lifetime experiences for the most discerning audience in the world. That doesn’t happen over Zoom. It happens through collisions: a spark across a desk, a kitchen-side conversation that unlocks a partnership, the energy of ideas felt, not typed. That’s why in-office culture is non-negotiable at Dorsia.

Who We Hire

We don’t subscribe to check-the-box hiring. We hire for merit and mindset, which naturally creates a team with varied backgrounds. What unites us isn’t demographics, it’s a shared vision: to build the social operating system for the cultural vanguard.

Lifestyle Hours

We’re not a 9-to-5 company. Our lifestyle mirrors our members. Early flights, after-work events, and late-night sprints when the work demands it. But we love what we do, and we definitely love a good party.

High Performance Culture

Working at Dorsia isn’t for everyone—and that’s the point. Our culture is designed for builders, not passengers. We move fast, set ambitious standards, and expect people to rise to them. If you have the talent and the drive, this will be a ride to remember.

A Final Word

We’re building something special. It will take long hours and relentless effort. It’s not for everyone. For those with the metabolism, you’ll create something that changes how culture is lived. And that’s the kind of work worth your life’s energy.

jobs.title: Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician - Green Bay, WI
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As an Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician, you’re part of a team that thrives on the front lines of emergency veterinary care where every second counts. You’ll handle a wide range of cases, from minor to complex emergencies, collaborating with our doctors and team in delivering gold standard, emotionally intelligent care. You’ll jump into triage, treatments, diagnostics, anesthesia, monitoring, and critical care nursing, all while being a steady, compassionate presence for pet parents in their most stressful moments. This role is for someone who wants to do the work they were trained to do (and more), continue growing their skills, and help people and their pets when they need it most.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Treat every patient and person like they matter—because they do! You keep people and pets together and stay by their side through tests, treatments, and everything in between

• Jump into action, delivering nursing care, treatments, and emotional support in the most critical moments, from triage to discharge

• Bring the meds, the monitoring, and the mastery—from IVs and CRIs to blood transfusions and beyond

• Communicate like a teammate and think like a leader, helping shape plans and keep care flowing

• Be ready to perform CPR like the trained RECOVER rockstar you are (not only do we offer training, we have the highest number of RECOVER CPR professionals and instructors in the industry!)

• All the techy stuff—from diagnostics and imaging to sample collection and placing tubes

• Anesthesia, even for our most fragile patients? You’ve got it.

• Use all the advanced techniques in your toolkit: central lines, endoscopy, ultrasounds, and more

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate’s degree or higher in veterinary technology from an AVMA accredited program strongly preferred

• Credentialed as a Veterinary Technician (CVT, RVT, LVT, LVMT) in the state the VEG practice is located is required; VTS in ECC, internal medicine or anesthesia/analgesia is a plus and will lead to extra considerations in compensation

• 1+ years of experience in a veterinary technician role; experience in emergency or specialty medicine preferred

• Basic computer skills and a comprehension of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. The Opportunity

The Quality Operations team is expanding and looking to hire a Manager of QC/AD, reporting to the Senior Director of QC/AD. This individual will be responsible for managing analytical development activities to support the Amylyx pipeline products including synthetic peptides, antisense oligonucleotides and small molecules. This individual will support phase appropriate analytical development, qualification/validation and oversight of GMP release and stability testing. The ideal candidate will be a motivated, self-starter, well versed in the GMPs, willing to actively collaborate cross functionally and excited about the potential to deliver therapies to patients in need.

Responsibilities

• Support QC GMP systems by maintaining reference standard, critical reagent and method performance programs.
