jobs.title: Behavior Therapist
jobs.description:
Behavior Therapist

Aspire Living & Learning — Windsor, VT
Pay: $19.22–$25.43 per hour
Job Type: Full-time, year-round (Part-time also available!)
Schedule: Monday–Friday, between 7:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m.
Work Location: In person

Start a Rewarding Career as a Behavior Therapist

Aspire Living & Learning is hiring compassionate, dependable, and energetic Behavior Therapists to support children, adolescents, and young adults with developmental disabilities, including individuals on the autism spectrum.

This entry-level position provides hands-on experience in applied behavior analysis (ABA). No prior ABA experience is required. Aspire Living & Learning provides comprehensive on-the-job training, ongoing supervision, and support to help qualified employees pursue Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification.

Experience in customer service, sales, education, healthcare, business, human services, marketing, communications, maintenance, government, or another field may be valuable in this role.

About the Behavior Therapist Role

Behavior Therapists work under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) and/or special education teacher. You will implement individualized behavior support plans, education plans, and service agreements while helping clients develop communication, social, academic, motor, and daily living skills.

Clients may demonstrate mild to severe behavioral challenges, including aggressive or self-injurious behavior. The role requires patience, emotional maturity, physical fitness, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm in high-pressure situations.

Behavior Therapists may work in:

• Aspire Living & Learning clinics

• Public and private school settings

• Client homes, as assigned

• Community environments

Key Responsibilities

• Implement individualized behavior support plans using applied behavior analysis techniques

• Teach communication, social, motor, play, cognitive, and self-care skills

• Support clients with daily living and personal care routines

• Reduce challenging behaviors through approved intervention strategies

• Collect accurate data on behavior, progress, and skill development

• Follow written treatment plans, protocols, and safety procedures

• Use prompting, discrete trial teaching, and naturalistic learning techniques

• Apply prevention, redirection, and physical intervention procedures when necessary and properly trained

• Maintain focus and attention for extended periods

• Collaborate with behavior analysts, special education teachers, families, and other team members

• Participate in team meetings, training sessions, and ongoing supervision

• Adapt to daily schedule changes and changing client needs

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree preferred; a combination of college coursework and relevant experience may be considered

• Previous experience in ABA, education, healthcare, human services, behavioral health, or direct support is helpful but not required

• Valid driver’s license

• Reliable transportation

• Proof of automobile insurance

• Vehicle capable of transporting clients in the back seat

• Ability to travel within approximately 45 minutes of Windsor, Vermont

• Ability to pass a background check

• Strong communication and interpersonal skills

• Physical fitness and coordination

• Ability to demonstrate approved physical prevention and redirection techniques

• Willingness to assist with personal care routines when necessary

• Ability to manage multiple details and follow instructions accurately

• Flexibility to work Monday through Friday between 7:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m.

• Ability to respond professionally to day-to-day schedule changes

Compensation and Benefits

• Hourly pay: $19.22–$25.43, based on education and experience working under a BCBA

• Bachelor’s degree with no prior experience: $20.61 per hour

• Guaranteed year-round schedule of 37.5 hours per week

• Opportunities to work up to 40 hours per week, including meetings and training

Apply Today

Employees at Aspire enjoy working with a collaborative and dedicated team that values a culture of belonging and care. We take pride in offering a comprehensive benefits package to eligible employees, including:

• Comprehensive Health, Dental, & Vision Insurance - Choose from multiple medical plans, with vision coverage included at no extra cost.

• Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Health Saving Account (HSA) options - Use pre-tax dollars for medical and dependent care expenses.

• Lifestyle Spending Accounts with JOON - Monthly funds for wellness, fitness, commuting, childcare, pet care, and more.

• 403(b) Retirement Plan with Employer Match - A 100% match on contributions up to 2% of your salary.

• Generous Paid Time Off - Paid sick, personal, and vacation days, plus holidays.

• Professional Growth Opportunities - Access to training, leadership and management courses, mentorship, and career advancement.

• Employer-Paid Life & Disability Insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Telehealth Services and more!

If you want to join us in making a difference and positively impact the lives of others while charting your own path of development, then we at the Aspire team would love to hear from you.

Aspire Living & Learning believes it must play an active role in creating a community of employees that is diverse, inclusive and equitable. Our work benefits greatly from the contributions of people of color, people from working class backgrounds, women, LGBTQ people, and individuals with disabilities. Hence, we strongly encourage applications from people with these identities or who are members of other marginalized communities.

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Lyon, France
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The France Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-100,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Speechify is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace.

Speechify does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

jobs.description:

The Restaurant Manager is responsible for supporting the Restaurant Leader in day-to-day operations of the restaurant and upholding Raising Cane’s standards and culture in shift management responsibilities of restaurant operations.

The physical work environment includes working in a fast-paced kitchen environment (which requires extended periods of physical exertion, such as walking, standing, lifting and bending) and interacting with customers. • General to the role:Enforces Raising Cane’s policies and standardsExecutes shift management meeting Raising Cane’s operations and safety standardsUses required tools, forms and logs to support shift execution, document results and take corrective action when neededDirects crewmembers during a shiftProvides exemplary customer serviceUtilizes reward and recognition program for the crewmembers in the restaurantAuthorizes employee functions requiring manager approval (e.g. discounts, promotions, timeclock overrides, etc.)Ensures cleanliness of the restaurant and ensures the facility is in good working orderCompletes other duties as assigned

Requirements for Success:

• Detail-oriented, organized and able to manage multiple priorities that may be constantly changing
• Self-driven, flexible, and highly energetic with strong written and verbal communication skills
• Able to work effectively and efficiently both independently and collaboratively
• Able to recognize problems, set goals, execute and convert plans into action to solve problems
• Knowledge and skills in staffing, scheduling, people and cost management
• Proficient in a variety of technology systems including Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and Outlook) and ability to learn and adapt to new systems quickly
• Able to work a variety of shifts including days, evenings and weekends and travel as needed for work-related functions and training
• Must complete all required Raising Cane’s company training programs
• 1+ years of restaurant or retail management experience
• Must be 18 years of age or older
• High school diploma or equivalent preferred

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Privacy Policy

Candidate Privacy Notice

jobs.title: Senior Standard Cell Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are (video)

At JRC, we tackle some of the toughest challenges faced by the Department of Defense (DoD) and other government agencies. Our expertise in engineering innovation and semiconductor technologies allows us to deliver mission-critical microelectronics solutions, aerospace systems engineering, and cutting-edge research and development. By joining JRC, you’ll be part of a team that supports strategic deterrence and defense missions, playing a crucial role in ensuring the safety and security of the United States and its allies.

🚀Join JRC's Semiconductor Technology Team!

Join JRC’s cutting‑edge Semiconductor Technology team as a Senior Standard Cell Design Engineer and lead the development of next‑generation radiation‑hardened microelectronics. In this high‑impact role, you’ll drive the technical execution of our LEAP Standard Cell Library, shape proprietary simulation tools for radiation‑induced reliability prediction, and collaborate closely with foundry partners on advanced-node designs.

You’ll architect and validate new standard cells across multiple technologies, optimize PPA under extreme conditions, support MPW test‑chip runs, and advance key automation and modeling capabilities. This role is ideal for an engineer who thrives at the intersection of device physics, circuit design, and reliability modeling.

We’re looking for someone with deep semiconductor design expertise, hands‑on experience in standard cell and library development, strong simulation and characterization skills, and eligibility for a U.S. security clearance. Experience with advanced nodes, RHBD techniques, memory design, and characterization tools is a strong plus.

If you’re excited about building resilient microelectronics that power mission‑critical systems, we’d love to meet you.

💼What You'll Do

• Execute the design and development of Radiation Hardened LEAP Standard Cell Libraries across multiple advanced foundry technology nodes.

• Generate and validate new standard cells and IP, including combinatorial logic, sequential logic, and power management cells.

• Leverage in-house software and industry-standard SPICE tools to calculate radiation-induced error rates to ensure circuit resilience.

• Execute advanced library characterizations to optimize Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) in harsh environments.

• Collaborate directly with external foundry partners on Multi-Product Wafer (MPW) runs and provide technical design support to customers.

• Contribute to the development of proprietary simulation software and automation scripts to improve reliability prediction.

🧠What You Bring

• Master’s degree with 2+ years of direct industry experience, OR a Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of experience.

• Must be eligible to obtain a U.S. security clearance due to the nature of defense-related projects.

• Deep knowledge of semiconductor design methodologies and principles.

• Hands-on experience with standard cell design, circuit design, and layout, and associated design tools (e.g. Virtuoso, Spectre, HSPICE)

• Demonstrated experience being involved in test-chip designs and MPW execution.

• Proficiency in design flows including DRC/LVS, timing analysis, and power integrity.

• Extensive experience with simulation tools, specifically for library characterization.

⭐Bonus Points

• Master’s degree with 5+ years of experience, or Bachelor’s with 7+ years in industry.

• Hands‑on design experience with GAA nodes (e.g., Intel 18A), including device architecture and design‑rule familiarity.

• Proven background in SRAM/NVM bitcell design and/or memory compiler development.

• Practical experience with Liberate, PrimeLib, and SiSmart for characterization and modeling.

• Expertise in RHBD for SEE/SEU mitigation, plus proficiency in C++ and scripting (Python/TCL) across advanced nodes (FinFET, GAA, SOI).

At JRC we offer...

• A competitive compensation package

• An exceptional employee benefits program, providing support for our team members' well-being and success

• The chance to contribute to a high-profile Department of Defense programs and make a positive impact

• A collaborative work environment where teamwork, creativity, and innovation thrive

• Opportunities for professional growth and development, helping you advance your career

jobs.title: Product Engineer
jobs.description:
This role is part of a fast-growing AI company that is set to join saas.group, as one of our upcoming brands.

This role is attached to a future acquisition by saas.group. As the deal has not been officially announced yet, we can’t share the company name in this job post. We’ll tell you more about the company and product during the process.

We are an AI platform that turns images and text into ready-to-use 3D models in minutes, work that traditionally takes a 3D artist days or weeks. Game developers, 3D printing enthusiasts and creators use the platform to generate and edit images, turn them into 3D models in every major format, and chain it all together into their own pipelines. With more than 2 million registered users, we are now expanding into the business space, building custom AI workflows for companies such as 3D printing businesses.

Profile Overview

We’re looking for a Product Engineer who loves building products people enjoy using. You’ll work directly with our founder and take real ownership of the product: deciding what to build, shaping how it looks and feels, and shipping it end to end across frontend and backend.

This is not a role where you wait for tickets. You’ll have the freedom to drive the product yourself, used by a large and growing global user base, and a front-row seat as we move from hobbyists and indie game developers into business customers. If you have the craft and the taste, we’ll help you learn the 3D side.

Your immediate impact in the first 3-6 months will be:

• Ship new product features end to end, from the Next.js frontend to the Django backend.

• Keep the high UX and UI quality of the product as you ship new features, so everything new feels as polished as what's already there.

• Get up to speed on how 3D models, formats and pipelines work in our product.

• Take ownership of parts of the product and proactively propose what to build next.

Your responsibilities

• Own product features from idea to release, without needing a detailed spec for every task.

• Build refined, well-designed interfaces in Next.js (roughly 60% of the role).

• Implement and maintain backend features in Django and PostgreSQL (roughly 40% of the role), integrating third-party AI model APIs.

• Look after our servers and keep the platform reliable as we handle a lot of user data.

• Use AI coding tools daily to move fast without compromising quality.

What you bring to the table

• Full-stack experience: 5+ years building web products across frontend and backend.

• Tech stack: Strong experience with Next.js on the frontend and Django + PostgreSQL on the backend.

• Server management: Hands-on experience managing servers and working with Linux.

• Product taste: You know what a good product looks like, with an eye for clean UX/UI and the details (animations, shadows, polish) that make it feel great.

• Ownership: You’ve shipped a product with real users, ideally in a startup, as a founder or through your own side projects, and you’re used to driving things yourself.

• AI Literacy & Application: You actively use AI tools to enhance personal productivity and work quality, staying curious about emerging capabilities and identifying opportunities to apply AI pragmatically in day-to-day work.

Bonus points if you have:

• Experience with 3D models or the 3D space (meshes, formats, Blender, ideally Blender headless or similar pipeline work).

• Experience scaling a product.

• Experience with serverless GPU platforms such as Modal.

• Experience with Neon database, Celery or third-party AI model APIs.

No 3D experience yet? That’s fine: strong engineering and product skills come first, and we’ll help you get up to speed on the 3D side.

What’s in it for you

• Ultimate flexibility: We’re 100% remote. You can work from wherever you like, whenever you like.

• Freedom and autonomy: We’re a high-trust team, and you’ll be given lots of flexibility to solve problems in your own way, with plenty of help from the team when you need it.

• Minimum bureaucracy: We don’t like to get bogged down with meetings and red tape. We like to be efficient and keep momentum steady & sustainable.

• Small & friendly team: We help each other out, have fun, and joke around.

• Our network: We are a community of entrepreneurial SaaS professionals that regularly exchange ideas, knowledge, learning and expertise with each other internally.

Our future brand will be part of saas.group, and we have a shared goal of succeeding together.

jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Switzerland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-160,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Be part of the difference at NorthStar School of Innovation & Leadership! jobs.title: Head of Change Management Organizational Engagement
jobs.description:
Choreo is a wealth management firm built on an interconnected network of financial advisors with a shared vision servicing entrepreneurs, CPAs, and individuals with a forward-thinking approach to financial planning to translate wealth into fulfillment. With over 200 employees and 40+ locations across the country, we are here to serve our clients beyond what is expected.

OPENING SUMMARY

This role gives Choreo's people — and the client-facing teams at the center of the firm's growth — the confidence to move through change together. When this person succeeds, every major initiative affecting client-facing teams lands with clarity: people know what's changing, why it matters, and what's expected of them, well before it reaches their desk. Initiatives that once collided or moved out of sequence instead land with deliberate timing and a coherent plan behind them. Concerns and friction surface early, while there's still time to act on them. Leadership hears a clear, honest signal of what client-facing teams and employees are experiencing, and those teams can see that what they raised actually shaped a decision. Over time, change management becomes part of how Choreo runs every major initiative affecting its client-facing organization by default, not something applied after the fact.

Operating Principle:

This role works in close partnership with the Head of Brand & Communications, with each leader anchoring a distinct half of the same outcome. The Head of Brand & Communications leads what Choreo is saying, what it means, and how it comes to life at the enterprise level. This role leads how people — especially client-facing teams — experience, influence, and adopt the changes behind it.

Key Responsibilities:

Change management and adoption

• Build change management plans for major enterprise initiatives, with particular emphasis on those affecting client-facing teams, including stakeholder and impact assessments, readiness diagnostics, and reinforcement plans

• Define what strong adoption looks like for each initiative in measurable terms, and track it through to completion — with client-facing adoption as a primary lens

• Sequence and coordinate concurrent change initiatives so client-facing teams move through them with clarity and momentum, without competing demands colliding at the point of delivery

• Surface resistance, confusion, and unresolved dependencies among client-facing teams early, while there's still time to address them

Client-facing communications and engagement

• Own the communications strategy and operating rhythm for client-facing teams affected by change — sequencing, channel discipline, and message relevance across concurrent initiatives

• Coordinate communications to client-facing teams across transformation, technology, service, and growth initiatives so messaging is consistent and well-timed

• Build feedback loops that give client-facing teams a real opportunity to shape initiatives, and show them what their input changed

Human integration (M&A and organizational change)

• Build a repeatable methodology for the human side of mergers, acquisitions, and major organizational integrations, with specific attention to newly joined client-facing teams

• Lead the adaptive work around identity, culture, and belonging for newly joined or acquired client-facing teams

• Track the lived experience of integrated client-facing teams over time, well beyond the point of close

Organizational listening

• Build and run listening mechanisms before, during, and after major change, with client-facing teams as a primary audience — pulse surveys, structured interviews, focus groups

• Synthesize what's heard into a small number of clear themes and concrete recommendations for leadership

Change governance and infrastructure

• Establish the intake, prioritization, and escalation process that governs how change initiatives move through the firm, with clear checkpoints for anything reaching client-facing teams

• Define decision rights and change-readiness criteria that initiative owners are expected to meet before launch, especially for initiatives touching client-facing teams

• Build the standing methodology, templates, and measurement framework that make change management repeatable across initiatives, independent of any one project team

Required Qualifications:

• 8+ years of experience in change management, organizational effectiveness, or a closely related discipline, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise-scale initiatives affecting client-facing organizations

• Direct experience owning communications strategy and cadence for a large organization, spanning both internal (employee) and client-facing audiences

• Direct experience leading the human/organizational side of M&A integration, including the post-close experience of client-facing teams

• Hands-on experience designing and running organizational listening mechanisms for client-facing populations and translating results into leadership recommendations

• Strong program management discipline: scope definition, milestone tracking, risk mitigation, and stakeholder reporting across multiple concurrent workstreams

• Experience establishing change governance — intake, prioritization, and decision rights — across a portfolio of concurrent initiatives

• Strong executive presence; ability to influence and align senior stakeholders without formal authority over them

• Comfortable operating with ambiguity and shifting priorities in a fast-growing, actively integrating organization

• Experience in financial services, wealth management, or an RIA environment, with direct exposure to advisor or client-facing populations

• Change management certification (Prosci or equivalent), or demonstrated equivalent hands-on expertise

Success Measures

• Adoption of major initiatives improves among client-facing teams, measured against a defined baseline for each rollout

• Time-to-adoption shortens; friction and rework on priority programs decrease, particularly for initiatives touching client-facing teams

• Changing governance (intake, prioritization, readiness criteria) is used consistently across initiative owners

• Listening to data from client-facing teams becomes a recurring input to leadership decision-making

• Integrated client-facing teams (post-M&A) show measurable improvement in retention and engagement relative to pre-integration baselines

Critical Attributes

• Deep understanding of organizational behavior and changing adoption principles, particularly among client-facing populations

• Skilled at bringing clarity and sequencing complex, high-stakes situations

• Build trust and followership quickly across all levels, including with client-facing leaders

• Resilient and adaptive in a fast-paced, still-forming function

Employee Benefits

At Choreo, we provide a holistic, total reward offering to empower our teams in their professional and personal lives. We seek to provide employees with benefits that place an emphasis on health, happiness, and financial security. Here is what we offer:

• Competitive salary and bonus plan

• Competitive medical, dental, and vision plans

• Basic life and disability coverage

• 401(k) matching program

• Financial support for approved designations and courses

• Technical, leadership, sales training opportunities

• Unlimited, discretionary time off

• Paid parental leave

​​Choreo is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity, and inclusion.

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Lisbon, Portugal
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Portugal Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-65,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Stockholm, Sweden
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Sweden Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-115,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Dedicated Infrastructure
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

You'll lead GitLab's Dedicated Infrastructure team, combining hands-on technical leadership with team development. Working with the team's Product Manager, you'll balance delivery speed and quality, guide architecture decisions, and lead the team through incidents.

You'll demonstrate ideas through proofs of concept, give team members meaningful feedback, and use data to make prioritization and risk decisions.

What you’ll do

• Partner with the team's Product Manager to set clear priorities and deliver with quality and speed.

• Maintain at least 99.9% availability for Dedicated infrastructure, strengthen security, and automate operations to support more tenants at scale.

• Give your team clear direction and meaningful feedback, and build shared ownership of development and operations.

• Improve the platforms and tools your team owns so feature implementers can manage their services in production through self-service workflows.

• Recruit, onboard, and develop productive team members, supporting their growth and accountability.

• Lead by example with proofs of concept and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted approaches. Simplify processes and automate repetitive manual work.

• Model effective incident management, lead timely resolution and escalation, and document and teach best practices across GitLab.

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Bucharest, Romania
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Romania Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-80,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Speechify is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace.

Speechify does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Field Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT AVOCA

Avoca is transforming how home service companies engage with their customers. Our AI-powered conversational agents handle every high-value inbound call, from booking jobs, qualifying leads, and driving higher revenue, all at a speed and consistency unmatched by human call centers.

We're a Series B startup backed by Kleiner Perkins, Meritech Capital, General Catalyst, and other top-tier investors, with $125M raised and a $1B valuation. We grew 10x in 2025 and have scaled to 170+ employees in under two years across our NYC headquarters and Santa Barbara office.

In a $1T+ market where 85% of missed calls go to competitors, we're building the category-defining platform for AI-driven customer engagement, serving the largest brands in home services. With high-energy, in-office teams in both locations, every hire here has an immediate and visible impact.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Field Engineer on the Pre-Sales team, you'll be the technical builder behind how we win and enable deals. You'll own two things: the integration work that proves technical feasibility to prospects and partners during the sales cycle, and the demo tooling that lets the entire go-to-market team tell a credible, product-accurate story.

You'll work at the intersection of Sales, Partnerships, Product, Engineering, and AI, partnering with Account Executives and the Partnerships team as their technical counterpart. Unlike our Sales Engineers, who lead the customer-facing technical narrative, this role goes a layer deeper on the build: you're the person who can actually stand up a working integration against an unfamiliar API and turn it into a repeatable demo asset. This is a pre-sales role: you won't carry a closing quota, but your work directly determines whether technical buyers and integration partners trust that Avoca does what we say it does.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own technical scoping and feasibility for pre-sales opportunities and partner integrations; turning ambiguous requirements from prospects, partners, and AEs into concrete, working implementation plans.

 - Build working integrations against third-party APIs, CRMs, field service management (FSM) platforms, telephony systems, and partner ecosystems, writing real code, handling REST APIs, JSON, authentication, and webhooks, and getting a credible proof of concept working quickly.

 - Build and maintain the demo and sandbox tooling the GTM org relies on: reusable demo environments, representative fixture data, and internal tools, treating one-off deal builds as reusable assets (integration patterns, reference implementations, scripts) rather than throwaway work.

 - Configure and tune Avoca's conversational AI for demo and POC scenarios, including prompt engineering to reflect real customer workflows.

 - Serve as the technical counterpart to Account Executives and Partnerships in the room with a prospect's or partner's engineering team, establishing credibility from the C-suite to individual developers, and translating those conversations into plans a non-technical AE can run with.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues that surface during evaluations, pilots, and POCs, protecting at-risk deals and partner launches.

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to feed recurring integration gaps and field learnings back into the roadmap, and to keep demo environments current as the product evolves.

 - Partner with (not replace) Forward Deployed Engineering and Implementation when a build needs to graduate from a working POC to a hardened production deployment: you own the pre-sales build and the demo layer; production delivery is a handoff.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 4+ years in a technical, customer-facing role: Solutions/Sales Engineering, Forward Deployed / Deployment Engineering, Implementation or Integration Engineering, Solutions Consulting, or software engineering with meaningful customer exposure.

 - Hands-on ability to build. Proficient in TypeScript/JavaScript (Next.js, React, Node/Fastify); ships production-grade code and independently stand up an integration or demo tool, not just spec one for someone else to build. You don't need to be a production backend engineer, but "can build it yourself" is the bar.

 - Practical experience integrating against third-party APIs and enterprise systems: REST, JSON, authentication/OAuth, webhooks, and comfort working from unfamiliar or incomplete API documentation.

 - Working SQL and a solid grasp of relational data: enough to model, transform, and wire up realistic data for integrations and demo environments.

 - Experience owning something technical end-to-end, from requirements through build, testing, and a working rollout, even if handed off afterward.

 - Strong technical judgment and troubleshooting instincts, and the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

 - A product mindset toward internal tooling: you treat demo and sandbox infrastructure as a product with users (the GTM team).

 - Familiarity with AI-powered products, conversational AI platforms, or data-driven systems. Bonus: prompt engineering, call center / communications platforms, CRM or FSM integrations, or prior Partnerships/channel support experience.




WHO YOU ARE

 - Self-motivated, entrepreneurial, and comfortable operating in fast-moving, high-growth environments.

 - A builder who thrives on owning things end-to-end and turning one-off work into something reusable.

 - Autonomous, self-directed, and comfortable with ambiguity and incomplete requirements.

 - A proactive, effective communicator who's equally credible with a customer's engineers and your own AEs.

 - In-office, engaged, and eager to collaborate at our NYC location full-time.




BENEFITS

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Company-sponsored 401(k) through Vestwell

 - Flexible PTO plus U.S. federal holidays

 - Company-wide off-sites

 - Daily in-office lunch through Parkday

 - Monthly wellness stipend

 - Dinner covered when working late

 - Commuter benefits and late-night rideshare

 - Standing desks and workspace accommodations available on request

 - All core tools and software provided

Compensation: The expected base salary for this role is $160,000-$200,000 with final compensation based on experience, skills, and qualifications determined during the interview process. Avoca’s total compensation package includes base salary, bonus, equity, and a comprehensive suite of benefits and perks. Our Recruiting team will share the full details as you progress through our hiring process.




WHY AVOCA

At Avoca, you’ll be part of a team that’s building a category-defining company at the center of a massive market opportunity. We’re a fast-moving, collaborative team with a culture designed for builders who thrive on speed, iteration, and impact.



Avoca provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability.

jobs.title: Plant Operator Trainee
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

Under the direction of the Operations Supervisor, Operations Lead Personnel and in coordination of fellow Operations Personnel the incumbent will perform a variety of basic tasks relevant to the day-to-day operation of the wastewater treatment plant facilities, processes and equipment, including process and equipment rounds, recording operations data and information, making observations and reporting on variations in operating conditions, maintaining logs and other required reports and forms, and provides input for corrective actions and implements corrective actions as directed. Assist Operations in efforts to maintain efficient and cost-effective facility operations while maintaining compliance with all Corporate and Regulatory environmental, health and safety rules and requirements.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Works a scheduled shift and will be subject to required emergency call in or shift coverage as Operational needs demand.
• Under the direct Supervision of Shift Supervisor or Lead person may be required to perform some of the following tasks depending on the station assigned for that shift:Record and Read meters for (pumps, gauges, motors etc.…) in accordance with all regulatory requirements.Record tank levels, sludge blanket levels.Operate equipment pertinent to assigned workstation (GBT, BFP, overhead lifting jib crane, pumps)Open, close and adjust valves for tanks & pumps.Observe their process areas (pumps, motors, valves, sewage color, odor, flow) record their findings.Collect samples for laboratory analysis.Receive chemicals in bulk, drum and tote form.Adjust / bleed pumps as directed.Keep the workstation and surrounding area safe and clear of debris.Inspect equipment for proper functionality and refer to Maintenance for any necessary repairs.Maintain a logbook for the station they are operating.Create work requests for equipment found to be malfunctioning or broken.Make adjustments to equipment to optimize the operation (GBT & Dewatering).Troubleshoot operational issues and get approval of operations supervisor before executing.

Work Environment:

• Work is performed both inside and outside with exposure to all kinds of weather conditions.
• Incumbents may be occasionally exposed to some noise, silica, dust, fumes, smoke, gasses, greases, oils, electrical energy, solvents and vibration.
• Incumbents may work on slippery/uneven surfaces, around machinery with moving parts, moving objects/vehicles, ladder/scaffolding, below ground and may be exposed to water or other liquid materials.
• Maintain a high level of focus on health, safety and environment, ensuring safety within all activities.

Education/Experience/Background:

• High School Diploma or GED, associate degree (or equivalent experience) in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology/Laboratory or related fields preferred.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Requires good reading, math, writing, and verbal communication skills.
• Ability to read, and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles, and other equipment.
• Ability to understand/execute written and oral instructions, read/understand technical instructions.
• Ability to interpret data and information from technical service manuals and drawings.
• Knowledge of Windows, Google Workspace, MS Office Suite, and other computer-based systems.
• Knowledge of basic laboratory sampling, testing and documentation.
• Ability to adjust chemical feeds and processing equipment as directed to maintain compliance.
• Basic knowledge of wastewater treatment equipment and processes.
• Must have the ability to maintain effective working relations w/management, supervisors, and staff.
• Must be able to work as a team in a teamwork-oriented environment.
• Must be safety conscious and able to work independently with little or no supervision.
• Must have a general understanding of how the treatment plant works and the SPDES limits associated to the station being operated.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Valid NYS Driver’s license and the ability to meet risk management guidelines.
• Ability to attend classes required for obtaining valid NY State Wastewater Treatment license and obtain license within 24 months.

Pay Rate: $22.91 per hour.

Benefits: Our employees are covered by comprehensive benefits packages including paid time off policies; health, dental, vision, and life insurance; retirement plans, savings accounts; tuition reimbursement; paid volunteering and more.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION

Join us in shaping the future of paid search intelligence.

Adthena is an award-winning search intelligence platform powered by patented AI technology and a team of dedicated experts. We help brands, marketers, and agencies dominate their competitive landscapes with unparalleled insights into the paid search market. Our Whole Market View, Smart Monitor, and Local View solutions give clients the clarity to optimize spend, increase ROI, and stay ahead of the competition.

Trusted by global brands like Citibank, L’Oréal, and Volvo, and backed by Updata Partners, we’ve been redefining search intelligence since 2012. 

In 2025, Adthena continued its winning streak, earning 8 major search industry awards. Highlights include Best AI Search Software Solution at the US Search Awards, Best Search Software Tool at the European Search Awards, and Best Software Innovation at the Global Search Awards.

Ready to make an impact in an industry-leading company? Let’s do it together.




WHY JOIN US?

We offer the best of both worlds: the maturity and stability of a well-established company combined with the energy, agility, and impact of a scaling tech organisation.

We’re smaller than large-scale enterprises, offering more autonomy, less red tape, and accelerated growth.




HERE’S WHAT WE OFFER:

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Warsaw, Poland
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Poland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-110,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!
