jobs.title: VP, Product Engineering
jobs.description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

To flourish here, you must be prepared to set a high bar for yourself and those around you. There is always a way to contribute: Acting with autonomy, having accountability and being open to new perspectives are essential to our continued success.

Our deep curiosity to learn and our eagerness to share diverse passions with others gives us balance and injects a one-of-a-kind vibrancy into our culture.

If you are driven to solve exhilarating challenges and have a bias toward action in the face of change, you will be empowered to make a real impact here, with a sharp and passionate team at your back. If Braze sounds like a place where you can thrive, we can’t wait to meet you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

We are in search of a VP of Engineering for our Channels division, the action layer of the Braze technology platform. Our channels are where the Braze platform meets the end user, where our customers create rich messaging that is delivered to their end users via our channels: Email, Push, SMS/MMS/RCS, WhatsApp, LINE, In-App Messages, Content Cards, Banners, Landing Pages, Feature Flags, Webhooks, and more to come.

You will lead this multi-team division through its next stage of technical and product transformation. This role presents formidable engineering challenges that call for a collaborative and cross-functional approach, necessitating close coordination with product and design teams. You will manage the team and help to grow the organization, leading software engineering via architecture design, growing engineering teams and skillsets, setting vision and goals, process and protocol, and hiring. On the product front - you will solve a number of interesting problems, from developing highly differentiated and sophisticated channel products, to thinking about how we build and position the broad portfolio of channels. On the engineering front - maturation of our systems into a more modular, efficient technology platform, all while delivering best-in-class product, is a major goal. And across both fronts, you will lead this organization through the AI transition: channel products that are increasingly intelligent and agentic, and an engineering org that leverages AI-assisted development to raise its own velocity and quality bar.

WHO YOU ARE

• Several years of relevant experience as a manager of experienced managers with a strong track record of transformative success

• A durable, motivated, ambitious, high-energy leader

• A great people leader, capable of growing a world class team

• A great technical leader, who can operate at different levels of granularity, from high level vision to partnering on detailed technology decisions

• Deep credibility in large-scale distributed systems, with the ability to go toe-to-toe with senior engineers on architecture, reliability, and cost efficiency

• Fluent in AI-assisted engineering, with an informed point of view on how AI agents and tooling change the way engineering organizations build, operate, and are shaped

• A great process leader, who understands when to add and remove processes to help the org execute the best it can

• An excellent communicator and writer, whose impact and leadership is obvious in the artifacts they create to guide their team

For candidates based in the United States, the pay range for this position at the start of employment is expected to be between $284,762 and $480,536/year with an expected On Target Earnings (OTE) between $320,000 and $540,000/year (including bonus or commission). Your exact offer may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to cash compensation, this role qualifies for a comprehensive Total Rewards package that includes equity grants of restricted stock (RSUs) so that you will own a piece of our company.

WHAT WE OFFER

jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Sofia, Bulgaria
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Bulgaria Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-55,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

Speechify does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Associate Director - Payer Strategy Enablement, U.S. Market Access
jobs.description:
The Associate Director, Payer Strategy Enablement will support the U.S. Market Access Payer Strategy organization by driving strategic planning, operational excellence, and execution of key business priorities across therapeutic areas and customer segments. This individual will serve as a trusted partner to Payer Strategy leaders, helping strengthen organizational effectiveness, enhance cross-functional coordination, and drive consistency across the Market Access organization. The role will lead development and management of common processes, reporting tools, planning resources, and governance mechanisms that improve visibility, alignment, and execution while enabling Payer Strategy leaders to focus on customer strategy, market dynamics, and business priorities. The position offers broad exposure to Market Access strategy, contracting, customer engagement, emerging market trends, and cross-functional leadership while playing a key role in shaping the future capabilities and operating model of U.S. Market Access.

Responsibilities:

Strategic Planning & Business Operations

• Support execution of annual strategic planning, business reviews, and priority-setting activities across Payer Strategy teams
• Coordinate planning cycles, key milestones, deliverables, and leadership priorities across multiple therapeutic areas
• Maintain visibility to strategic initiatives, customer priorities, and critical business activities across Market Access
• Partner with leadership to track progress against strategic priorities and identify opportunities for improvement

Organizational Effectiveness & Enablement

• Lead development and management of common reporting tools, dashboards, trackers, and planning resources across the Payer Strategy organization
• Establish scalable processes and ways of working that can be leveraged consistently across therapeutic areas
• Drive consistency in planning, reporting, governance, and execution across teams
• Support implementation and pull-through of Future Fit, capability-building, and process improvement initiatives
• Partner with Market Access training and learning organizations to define service models, roles, responsibilities, and engagement approaches that maximize organizational effectiveness and capability development

Deal & Market Access Coordination

• Coordinate forward-looking visibility to key contracting, pricing, customer, and access-related milestones
• Support cross-functional alignment across Payer Strategy, Finance, Pricing, Trade, APEX, Account Teams, and other partner functions
• Help identify risks, dependencies, and coordination opportunities requiring leadership attention
• Support effective governance and communication for complex cross-functional initiatives

Communications, Training & Engagement

• Coordinate leadership meetings, touchpoints, business reviews, and organizational communications
• Support development and management of training calendars, planning resources, and knowledge-sharing tools
• Drive consistency of information, best practices, and operating approaches across Market Access teams
• Support employee engagement, culture, and organizational effectiveness initiatives
• Partner with training teams to translate payer strategy, customer insights, market access trends, and business priorities into scalable field education and capability-building initiatives
• Support development, review, and deployment of payer strategy training materials, including coordination of MRL review processes and cross-functional stakeholder input to ensure timely execution

Education and Experience:

• Bachelor’s Degree required; MBA or Master’s Degree preferred
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in Market Access, Payer Strategy, Commercial Operations, Strategic Planning, Marketing, Sales Leadership, or a related commercial function
• Track record leading cross-functional initiatives from planning through execution
• Experience working effectively across matrixed organizations and influencing without direct authority
• Demonstrated project management, planning, organizational effectiveness, and business operations experience

Essential Skills and Competencies

Critical Success Factors

• Enable Payer Strategy leaders to focus on customer strategy, market dynamics, and business priorities rather than administrative coordination
• Improve consistency, visibility, and execution across therapeutic area and cross-portfolio payer strategy organizations
• Strengthen coordination among Payer Strategy, Account Teams, APEX, Pricing, Finance, and other key partner functions
• Drive accountability and pull-through of strategic priorities, Future Fit initiatives, and business planning activities
• Build scalable tools, processes, reporting, and ways of working that enhance organizational effectiveness across U.S. Market Access

Core Competencies

• Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to effectively engage senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders
• Ability to simplify complex issues and translate strategy into actionable plans and execution
• Exceptional planning, organization, and project management skills
• Strong analytical mindset and ability to synthesize information into meaningful business insights
• Experience building and managing reporting tools, dashboards, trackers, governance processes, and planning resources
• Proven ability to identify opportunities, solve problems, and drive execution in a dynamic environment
• Experience navigating complex matrix organizations and influencing without direct authority
• Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills across functions, therapeutic areas, and organizational levels
• Ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously and deliver results under tight timelines
• High degree of professionalism, organizational savvy, discretion, and attention to detail
• Self-starter with intellectual curiosity, adaptability, and continuous improvement mindset
• Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and business planning tools

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer – Frontend
jobs.description:
Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

We are seeking a Staff Frontend Software Developer who is passionate about creating advanced web applications that revolutionize healthcare. jobs.title: Team Lead, Android Core Product - Athens, Greece
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

• Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight

• Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features

• Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval

• Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself

• Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through

• Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear

• Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own

• Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out

• When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time

• Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out

• Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear

• Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless

• Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early

• Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team

• Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on

• Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests

• Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work

• Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them

• Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there

• Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows

• A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does

• A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster

• The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally

• Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for

• Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec

• Excellent communication skills

Bonus

• Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects

• Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

• Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

The Greece Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-55,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

Think you’re a good fit for this job?

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

jobs.title: Senior Editor, Editorial Review
jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide.

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Instructions

• Application Deadline: Monday October 19th, at 5:00 pm ET.

• Submission Instructions: Please submit a cover letter in addition to your resume answering the following question: How would you describe yourself as an editor?

Intro to Position

The Senior Editor, Editorial Review is part of a critically important team at NPR committed to providing additional editing support to our journalism and our journalists; to ensure that NPR maintains and solidifies its status as a trusted source of news and information for the American public.

As part of a team, the Senior Editor will review journalistic work from across the Content Division as a final look before air or publication. The focus is on ensuring excellence, fairness, accuracy and consistency of individual work and work across platforms, recognizing that formats, story selection and story-telling techniques for different platforms will and should vary, in service of specific audiences.

The ideal candidate is an  experienced journalist and editor with wide-ranging editorial experience, including expertise across different platforms and subject matter. They must be deeply curious, open-minded and flexible; be skilled at editing in a large, complex media organization where the topics and journalists vary greatly and where the deadlines and volume of content can be intense.

This editor will work a Sunday through Thursday shift, for the general hours of 10 a.m. to 7 p.m., although some flexibility is required for breaking news.

This role is an on-site role based in Washington, DC. The editor will be required to work onsite at a frequency set by their manager. There will be some flexibility to work remotely on occasion with manager approval.

This is a union-represented role covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with SAG-AFTRA.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff are defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.

Responsibilities

• Edit journalistic content for accuracy, fairness and consistency, as a final editorial review before air or publication. The level/kind of review will vary depending on the type of work it is, for what platform and the circumstances surrounding it; for example, is this a breaking news situation or a long-term enterprise story?

• Copy edit digital news stories, breaking news, long-form features and multiplatform pieces, digital videos for grammar, general factual accuracy, as well as AP and NPR style.

• Determine what kind of additional editing may be needed for specific stories, depending on their complexity or subject matter, and depending on what kind of review has already been done by legal, standards and practices editors or others.

• Collaborate closely with the main editors for all content you’re reviewing, as well as with the show/platform leads for which this content will appear.

• With guidance from the Managing Editor or Deputy Managing Editors for Editorial Review, understand the expected content coming through for review on a day-to-day basis so as to effectively manage your workflow.

• Work closely with the Managing Editors for News and Planning and the newsroom Deputy Managing Editors who are managing both coverage planning and breaking news coverage so that your work is integrated with theirs, and you can effectively work as partners.

• Work closely with the Managing Editor for Standards and Practices and other leaders to develop guidance on editorial matters and best practices for the division.

• Review and understand data provided by content analysts about the division’s collective body of work and the review team’s impact on it; act on the findings as appropriate.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

• At least 8 years of distinctive, original news reporting or editing experience on a national level.

• Demonstrated experience editing on multiple platforms and a familiarity with the different audience needs of individual platforms.

• Demonstrated excellence in editing breaking news, explanatory journalism and feature stories.

• Excellent communication skills and a track record of working on collaborative projects.

• Proven experience in editorial decision-making.

• Ability to handle multiple and complex projects simultaneously under stringent timeframes, with changing priorities/conditions.

• Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadline pressure.

• Demonstrated commitment to data analysis and its use in understanding the division’s work and in service of audiences.

• Deep understanding of NPR’s core values and public service mission.

• Passion for connecting with diverse audiences on a range of platforms.

• Proven ability to consistently work well with others.

• Positive approach to embracing change.

• Well-developed interpersonal skills, ability to get along with diverse personalities.

• Ability to respect input but ultimately be confident enough to take decisive action and take responsibility for said action.

Education Requirements

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent in work experience

Work Location & Requirements

• On-site: This is an on-site role based in Washington, D.C. The editor will be required to work onsite at a frequency set by their manager. There will be some flexibility to work remotely on occasion with manager approval.

Job Type

• This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S. based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $130,000-147,000 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR offers access to comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

Does this sound like you? If so, we want to hear from you.

#LI-ONSITE

The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Pay Range

$130,000—$147,000 USD

NPR is an Equal Opportunity Employer. NPR is committed to being an inclusive workplace that welcomes diverse and unique perspectives, all working toward the same goal – to create a more informed public. Qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, age, religion, religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions, lactation, and reproductive health decisions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, transgender status, gender non-conforming status, intersex status, sexual stereotypes, nationality, citizenship status, personal appearance, marital status, family status, family responsibilities, military status, veteran status, mental and physical disability, medical condition, genetic information, genetic characteristics of yourself or a family member, political views and affiliation, unemployment status, protective order status, status as a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking, or any other basis prohibited under applicable law.

If you are a person with a disability needing assistance with the application process, please reach out to employeerelations@npr.org.

You may read NPR’s privacy policy to learn about how NPR may handle information you submit with any application.

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Staff Software Engineer, Agentic Search
jobs.description:
Build AI contracting at enterprise scale. Ship it fast.

Ironclad is building AI on one of the most consequential datasets in enterprise software: over 2 billion contracts across thousands of the world's largest organizations. Contracts run every dollar, deal, and business relationship on the planet, and the AI transformation of this space is still largely uncharted. Engineers here are building agentic solutions to problems that haven't been solved yet, in a category that's still being defined. The feedback loop is short, the data is rich, and the people closest to the work are the ones deciding what gets built next. That ability to deliver impact quickly is why the the companies at the forefront of AI choose Ironclad to manage their contracts.

We’re consistently recognized as a leader in the industry: a Leader in the Forrester Wave and Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contract Lifecycle Management, a Fortune Great Place to Work, and one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Workplaces. Ironclad has also been named to Forbes’ AI 50 and Business Insider’s list of Companies to Bet Your Career On. We’re backed by leading investors including Accel, Y Combinator, Sequoia, BOND, and Franklin Templeton. For more information, visit www.ironcladapp.com http://www.ironcladapp.com or follow us on LinkedIn.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Ironclad's Intelligence Platform team owns Agent Assistant, Conversational Search, and Content Understanding — the systems that help customers and AI agents understand, find, and act on the right contract information. These are the flagship AI capabilities of our product, built and operated by a combined team of ML and ML infrastructure engineers.

We have multiple roles open, and are hiring a range of levels — Staff and Senior Staff. As a Staff or Senior Staff Engineer, Agentic Search, you'll own the architecture that combines LLMs and retrieval systems to answer complex, ambiguous questions about a customer's contracts, and you'll set the technical direction that other engineers across the AI organization build on. You'll partner closely with product, applied science, and engineering leaders to raise the company's search quality bar, and you'll bring the technical depth and eval-driven rigor to turn ambiguous problems into shipped, measurable improvements. Scope and ownership will be calibrated to level.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own agentic search architecture. Design and evolve the systems that combine LLMs and retrieval to produce optimal answers to complex or ambiguous questions.

 - Drive eval-driven development. Design and run the benchmarks and experiments that measure search quality, and use that feedback to continuously improve the system.

 - Raise the search quality bar. Contribute to and influence the company's overall search quality standard.

 - Own content understanding and ingestion. Turn raw documents into processed data that retrieval systems can consume, by building and using NLP/LLM models and pipelines.

 - Set technical direction. Define architectural decisions and technical direction that other engineers across the AI organization build on.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 10+ years building production systems, with a substantial portion in search, information retrieval, content understanding, or recommendation systems at meaningful scale.

 - Demonstrated depth in one of: learned/hybrid retrieval (lexical + vector + reranking), query understanding/NLU pipelines, or production LLM agent systems — ideally more than one.

 - Experience with search frameworks (Elasticsearch or equivalent — Solr, Vespa, OpenSearch; embedding search) in production, including relevance tuning and reranking.

 - Fluency with modern LLM APIs and multi-provider orchestration (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) — reasoning about token budgets, provider-specific tool-calling semantics, and prompt-caching trade-offs.

 - Experience building eval-driven workflows — offline benchmarks, regression detection, structured A/B comparison — as opposed to shipping and hoping.

 - Strong autonomy, ownership, and technical leadership across teams, including mentoring senior engineers and driving architectural decisions.

 - Comfortable operating in a dynamic, fast-paced, outcome-driven environment.


GREAT TO HAVE

 - Hands-on experience with post-training algorithms and infrastructure, including SFT and RL.

 - Experience with content understanding and/or information retrieval in structured-document-heavy domains.

 - Prior work on RAG systems involving data sources in different formats (Google Docs, PDFs, DOCX, etc.).





BASE SALARY RANGES

 - Staff: $188,000 - $235,000

 - Senior Staff: $220,000 - $270,000

The base salary range represents the minimum and maximum of the salary range for this position based at our San Francisco headquarters. The actual base salary offered for this position will depend on numerous factors, including individual proficiency, anticipated performance, and the location of the selected candidate. Our base salary is just one component of Ironclad's competitive total rewards package, which also includes equity awards (a new hire grant, along with opportunities for additional awards throughout your tenure), competitive health and wellness benefits, and a commitment to career growth and development.


US Full-Time Employee Benefits at Ironclad:

Company Description

We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.

Job Description

Olsson is seeking a licensed Electrical Engineer to join our Federal Engineering & Design Team. This role independently performs standard electrical engineering techniques and procedures while applying professional judgment to adapt and modify designs as needed. The Engineer receives direction on assignment objectives and complex features and is responsible for executing work using established plans, standards, and federal requirements.

This position contributes to the development of purposeful, high-quality electrical designs that support federal clients, including military, government, and mission-critical facilities. The Engineer collaborates closely with multidisciplinary teams to deliver reliable, code-compliant, and constructible solutions while supporting project scope, schedule, and budget.

As part of Olsson’s Federal Engineering & Design Team, this role plays an important part in delivering projects that serve national interests and improve the built environment.

Responsibilities:

• Performs electrical engineering duties related to the evaluation, design, and documentation of electrical systems for small to large-scale federal projects, including power distribution, lighting, grounding, and related building systems.

• Applies standard electrical engineering techniques, methods, and procedures to develop constructible, code-compliant designs while evaluating and proposing minor adaptations to meet project-specific needs.

• Prepares electrical calculations, drawings, specifications, technical reports, and cost estimates in accordance with applicable codes, federal standards, and agency requirements.

• Assists with preparation and coordination of project documents and maintains awareness of project scope, schedules, budgets, and deliverables.

• Coordinates electrical design elements with other engineering disciplines and internal project teams to support integrated project outcomes.

• Communicates project development and progress with project managers and may participate in coordination efforts with federal clients, contractors, and consultants.

• Performs process design calculations, analyzes engineering data, and supports feasibility evaluations for proposed electrical systems.

• Enters, maintains, and updates project information and documentation within Olsson’s project management systems in accordance with the firm’s Quality Management Program.

• Diagnoses and assists in resolving technical design issues and supports quality assurance and quality control processes throughout project execution.

• May provide technical guidance and oversight to less experienced engineers or technical staff as assigned.

• Travel and participation in project charrettes, design reviews, and value engineering conferences.

• May travel to project sites and work in varying terrain and weather conditions during different stages of construction.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

• Working collaboratively with others.

• Having ownership in the work you do.

• Using your talents to positively affect communities.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering.

• Professional Engineer (PE) license is required.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with project teams and stakeholders.

• Solid problem-solving, decision-making, and analytical skills.

• Working knowledge of applicable electrical codes, federal standards, and regulatory requirements, with the ability to research and apply requirements as needed.

• Advanced mathematical and analytical abilities related to electrical engineering design.

• Working knowledge of applicable design tools and technologies, such as AutoCAD and Revit.

Why join us:

• Contribute to projects that serve national interests and make a difference in communities.

• Enjoy flexible work arrangements, including remote options, to support your work-life balance.

• Thrive in a supportive culture that values professional development and teamwork.

At Olsson, your expertise drives progress on projects that matter. If you’re passionate about federal engineering and ready to elevate your career, we want to hear from you.

Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

jobs.title: Director, Change Management & Enablement
jobs.description:
Purpose

We are looking for a people-first change leader to serve as Director of Finance Transformation Change Management & Enablement. In this highly visible role, you will lead the people, process, and adoption strategy for Finance Transformation initiatives - including technology implementations, operating model redesign, process standardization, and culture evolution. This role will ensure Finance employees and leaders are equipped to adopt new ways of working, build required capabilities, and sustain change over time.

The role requires deep collaboration with Finance leaders, HR Business Partners, technology teams, and external vendors to deliver integrated solutions that drive business performance and will also be responsible for the development and execution of Finance-wide programs and strategies that enhance employee engagement and support the company’s business performance and growth objectives.

You will be a trusted advisor to the senior leaders, a strategic partner across functions and geographies, and a builder of organizational change capability at scale. This is a leadership role for someone who sees change as a competitive advantage and knows how to make it stick.

The successful candidate will translate Finance Transformation priorities into practical change, communication, training, and adoption plans that improve process effectiveness, employee readiness, and business performance.

Responsibilities

Strategy & Leadership

• Define and own the strategy, methodology and governance model, establishing a sustained organizational capability rather than a project add-on.
• Serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership on all major Finance Transformation initiatives.
• Lead, develop, and mentor a team of practitioners, fostering a high-performance culture.
• Champion a digital-first, data-driven approach to change, leveraging AI tools, analytics, and real-time adoption metrics.

Change Execution

• Lead end-to-end change management for Finance Transformation programs including technology transformations and strategic culture initiatives.

• Develop and execute integrated change management plans: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessments, readiness assessments, communication strategies, and training/capability building programs.

• Partner with Finance process owners to translate process changes into clear roles, behaviors, training needs, adoption plans, and success measures.

• Identify and proactively manage resistance, change fatigue, and adoption barriers across diverse employee populations.

• Drive cultural alignment efforts, particularly in support of transformation programs.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

• Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors, functional leaders, HR business partners, and front-line managers to embed change management best practices.

• Design and execute multi-channel, audience-specific communication campaigns that create clarity, build belief, and inspire action.

• Facilitate executive alignment sessions, workshops, and other forums to accelerate decision-making and coalition building.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

• Define and track KPIs for change adoption, employee engagement, readiness, and sustained behavior change.

• Use real-time data, pulse surveys, and sentiment analysis to continuously refine change strategies and report progress to senior leadership.

• Codify lessons learned and embed them into an evolving Finance Organizational Change Management (OCM) playbook.

Required Experience

• 10-15+ years of progressive experience in organizational change management, organizational effectiveness, or enterprise transformation.
• Demonstrated success leading change management for enterprise-scale programs (ERP, M&A, operating model redesign, digital transformation).
• Proven ability to influence and advise C-suite and senior executive stakeholders without formal authority.
• Experience building and scaling change management teams, centers of excellence, or enterprise change capabilities.
• Deep expertise in a wide range of change management methodologies - Prosci/ADKAR, Kotter, McKinsey Influence Model or equivalent.
• Strong project management discipline, with the ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously and deliver results on time; PMP or equivalent certification a plus.
• Experience working in matrixed, global, complex organizations.
• Exceptional communication skills (written, verbal, presentation) with executive presence and ability to facilitate engaging learning experiences.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Experience

• Familiarity with AI-enabled change tools and digital adoption platforms.

Education

• Bachelor's degree required in Organizational Psychology, Business, Communications, HR, or a related field.
• Master's degree preferred (MBA, I/O Psychology, Organizational Development).
• Prosci Change Practitioner Certification strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Client Success
jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

About the Role

The Senior Director, Client Success leads client experience strategy and team performance across the full account portfolio. This role owns the strategic direction, financial performance, and long-term retention of Datavant’s client relationships across every tier, while building and scaling the talent, governance, and processes that enable the broader Client Success organization to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes. The Senior Director partners with executive stakeholders, internally and externally, up to the C-suite, to translate market, regulatory, and competitive insight into proactive strategy, and serves as a strategic connector across Sales, Product, Operations, and Technology.

What You Will Do

Strategic Thinking & Solutioning

• Guide strategy across accounts within your scope aligning client roadmaps to Datavant corporate and Business Unit priorities.

• Anticipate market shifts, regulatory changes, and competitive pressures, translating insight into proactive, scalable strategies.

• Guide the team in prioritizing high-impact initiatives, balancing financial performance, operational feasibility, and long-term client value.

• Identify and act as a change agent for business process improvements — leveraging process engineering, AI, Business Intelligence, and Third-Party Organization (TPO) partnerships to drive transformation.

Leadership Excellence

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of CSMs, Senior CSMs, and Managers, setting a clear vision and driving alignment across large, complex teams.

• Build scalable talent strategies, succession plans, and performance standards that elevate the broader Client Success organization.

• Engage regularly with executive stakeholders, internally and externally, influencing outcomes and serving as a strategic connector across functions.

• Excel at talent acquisition, including onboarding and retention, to continually raise the talent bar.

Client Experience Management & Influential Communication

• Own executive relationships across the account portfolio, acting as a trusted advisor to stakeholders up to the C-suite.

• Oversee delivery strategy across implementations, renewals, growth, and escalations, ensuring a consistent, high-quality client experience.

• Coach leaders to deliver compelling executive presentations, manage change effectively, and drive alignment through clear, outcome-focused communication.

Business & Industry Acumen (Growth-Oriented)

• Apply deep healthcare, risk adjustment, and retrieval expertise to shape client strategy and identify expansion opportunities across complex enterprise accounts.

• Own full-cycle management of a portfolio of accounts, achieving revenue, retention, and growth goals through effective execution and partnership plans.

• Connect industry trends, product capabilities, and financial performance to long-term growth plans; leverage financial awareness to translate strategy into action.

• Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Operations leadership to influence roadmap decisions and drive sustainable revenue and retention outcomes.

Execution

• Be accountable for execution across the full account portfolio ensuring operational efficiency, delivery excellence, and predictable results.

• Establish governance models and scalable frameworks that drive consistency across the Business Unit.

• Take decisive action to remove systemic barriers, resolve high-impact issues, and ensure commitments translate into measurable client value.

Data Driven

• Champion a data-driven culture across large portfolios, setting KPIs that align client performance with corporate growth goals.

• Use analytics and financial insights to inform strategy, mitigate risk, and optimize outcomes.

• Use data to tell a story and deliver compelling, executive-ready presentations that influence key stakeholders.

• Coach the team to leverage data effectively, translating complex metrics into clear executive narratives that influence decisions and future direction.

What You Will Bring to the Table

• 10+ years of progressive experience in client success, account management, or strategic consulting within healthcare, health insurance, or healthcare data/technology, including 5+ years of people leadership managing managers or multi-level teams.

• Deep subject-matter expertise in Risk Adjustment and Retrieval processes, SLA frameworks, and the Payer/Provider/Vendor ecosystem; working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare data privacy requirements.

• Demonstrated success managing executive-level (up to C-suite) relationships within large, complex enterprise accounts.

• Proven track record owning revenue, retention, and growth targets for a multi-million-dollar portfolio.

• Experience building and scaling talent strategies, succession plans, and performance standards across multi-level teams.

• Strong financial acumen; able to translate data and market insight into strategy, investment decisions, and risk mitigation.

• Advanced proficiency with data/BI tools (e.g., Excel, Power BI, SQL) and the ability to translate complex metrics into executive-ready narratives.

• Exceptional presentation, negotiation, and executive communication skills; comfortable driving alignment across Sales, Product, Operations, and Technology leadership.

• Demonstrated ability to lead through organizational change, ambiguity, and competing priorities.

• BA/BS degree or equivalent experience; advanced degree a plus.

Location: Venice, CA

Reports to: Assistant General Manager

Hourly Rate: $30.00

Department: Food & Beverage

The Lighthouse, part of Whalar Group, is a first-ever creative campus and studio playground for the Creator Generation, offering Creators an I.R.L. platform to Learn, Make, and Belong. With Venice, CA already opened, and Brooklyn, NY opening in Fall 2025, and London/EMEA opening in 2026, the campuses are designed to empower and support career Creators and creative professionals, providing a dynamic environment explicitly tailored to their needs. Each campus features state-of-the-art, mixed-use content studios, and hosts impactful programming that empowers members to collaborate, learn, and grow their businesses within a thriving community.

The Lighthouse expands opportunities and creative capabilities, offering Creators a dedicated space to co-create, connect, and lead the businesses shaping creative culture. Learn more: www.thelighthouse.com.

About the role:

The café at The Lighthouse is an important part of the daily rhythm of our campus, a place where members start their mornings, take meetings, connect with one another, and return to throughout the day.

We’re looking for a Café Lead who is deeply passionate about coffee, genuinely loves hospitality, and is excited to help shape an exceptional café experience within The Lighthouse.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll make incredible coffee, understand the science and craft behind it, anticipate what members and guests need before they ask, and create thoughtful hospitality touches that make people feel known and cared for.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

• Prepare consistently exceptional coffee and beverages.

• Maintain deep knowledge of coffee, extraction, equipment, technique, and product quality.

• Create a warm, highly hospitable experience for members, guests, and regulars.

• Learn member preferences and anticipate needs in a membership-based environment.

• Own café inventory, including ordering, receiving, stock levels, storage, waste control, and regular inventory counts.

• Maintain café cleanliness, organization, presentation, and readiness.

• Help establish café standards, systems, and service rituals.

• Train and support additional café team members.

• Partner with the broader team on events, programming, and member experiences.

• Assist with integrating a thoughtful, high-quality food program into the overall café experience.

Here’s what we’re looking for:

• Serious coffee expertise and genuine curiosity about the craft and science of coffee.

• Strong barista experience and confidence operating café equipment.

• Exceptional hospitality instincts: warm, observant, proactive, and detail-oriented.

• Comfort building relationships with frequent members and regular guests.

• Ability to balance speed, consistency, and high standards.

• An owner’s mentality and excitement about helping shape what the café experience at The Lighthouse can become.

The Perks:

• Medical, Dental, Vision

• PTO + Sick Time

• HSA, FSA, and Commuter + Parking Benefits

• Company Paid Life & Disability Insurance

• Voluntary Life Insurance Policy

• Voluntary Hospital and Critical Illness Insurance

• Employee Assistance Program

• 401k with Employer Matching. No Vesting Period.

Our values:

At The Lighthouse, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) isn't just a statement, it's our collective strength. Our people are our superpower. A diverse team and inclusive leadership have shaped Whalar since our inception in 2016, fueling a constant evolution of growth. We champion a culture of respect and empathy, fostering a sense of belonging that transcends demographics. We hire individuals of all backgrounds and empower them to thrive, challenge stereotypes, and actively break societal barriers.

The Lighthouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. jobs.title: Preventive Maintenance Field Technician (PM Mechanic)
jobs.description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Preventive Maintenance Field Technician (PM Mechanic)

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We’re hiring a Preventive Maintenance Field Technician (PM Mechanic) at our onsite facility in Pasadena, TX, and we’re looking for someone who’s ready to grow with us, bring energy and drive to their work, provide maintenance and repair for a variety of company owned heavy equipment machinery and aerial lifts and help us build the future of construction. Mechanics will have the opportunity to work on the newest fleet in the industry.

Schedule: Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM, and offers overtime pay after working 40 hours. (This role is subject to on-call scheduling with additional compensation provided)

Primary Responsibilities

As a Field Technician, you’ll use our tech to create, assign, and monitor work orders, track machine service intervals, order parts, and diagnose issues faster by pulling data from hundreds of makes and models. With real-time information at your fingertips, you can determine the root cause and corrective action for each issue quickly, enabling you to work smarter, not harder.

• Practice safe job practices for repairing equipment

• Use technology (laptops and tablets) comfortably

• Maintenance and repair of complex mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and diesel systems on a variety of rental and customer equipment and tools while using a high degree of independent judgment

• Assist in the training of lower level technicians as needed

• Maintain paperwork/electronic documentation of work performed (work orders) in a complete and timely manner on a daily basis

• Assist with pick-up and delivery of equipment & parts

• Be knowledgeable of OSHA requirements (preferred)

• Field Mechanic: When required, travel to customer job sites for repair/maintenance of rental or customer owned equipment; must maintain service vehicle in a clean and professional manner

• Year-round company provided OEM training

• Other duties, assigned as needed

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Monthly Family Dinner Night — We treat you and your family to dinner every month, because family comes first. (An employee favorite!) *restrictions apply

• Competitive compensation

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• 401(k) + company match

• Tool and boot reimbursements (role dependent)

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events, food truck nights, and monthly team dinners

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

• Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities

• Access to industry leading diagnostic tools

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

Required Skills/Abilities:

• Must own tools applicable to position

• Advanced mechanical aptitude and working knowledge of tools

• Extensive knowledge of construction equipment with an advanced understanding of schematics and diagrams

• Superior customer service, teamwork and verbal/written communication skills

Education and Experience:

• High School diploma, Trade school certificate preferred

• Experience in field service, maintenance and repair preferred

• Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record. Must be at least 21 years old to operate company vehicle.

Physical Requirements:

• Must be able to move, stand, stoop and bend freely

• Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times

• Field Technicians may be required to be clean shaven in order to enter worksites for EquipmentShare customers who have this requirement

• This is a safety sensitive position and any offer of employment will be contingent on passing a 10 panel drug screen

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an EOE M/F/D/V.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

The Change Management & Enablement Senior Manager plays a critical role in driving Finance Transformation programs forward as part of enterprise-wide culture and behavior change to enable sustainable adoption of new processes, ways of working, and operating models within AbbVie Finance.  This role goes beyond project delivery to focus on embedding change into the organization’s DNA, ensuring that employees not only adopt new tools and processes, but also embrace the mindsets, behaviors, and cultural shifts required to sustain transformation.

The individual will lead the design and execution of integrated change strategies that influence leadership alignment, employee engagement, and process adoption, ultimately accelerating value realization and long-term organizational effectiveness.

Responsibilities:

Culture & Behavior Change Leadership

• Lead Finance Transformation initiatives that drive mindset and behavior change, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and adaptability.

• Partner with senior leaders to model and reinforce desired cultural attributes and ways of working.

• Work with SMEs to translate transformation objectives into clear behavioral expectations and adoption milestones.

Process & Adoption Transformation

• Drive end-to-end adoption of new processes and operating models, ensuring alignment across people, process, and technology.

• Identify and address barriers to adoption, focusing on sustainable behavior change vs. one-time implementation.

• Embed change into business routines, governance forums, and performance management where appropriate.

Integrated Change Strategy & Execution

• Develop and execute holistic change strategies that integrate communications, training, stakeholder engagement, and reinforcement mechanisms.

• Apply structured change management methodologies to support both large-scale transformations and targeted process improvements.

• Ensure alignment of change activities across cross-functional teams and initiatives.

Stakeholder Engagement & Leadership Alignment

• Build strong, trusted partnerships with senior leaders and project teams to drive alignment, sponsorship, and accountability.

• Conduct stakeholder and readiness assessments to inform targeted interventions.

• Act as a strategic advisor to leaders on navigating organizational change and resistance.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

• Define and track adoption, behavior change, and culture metrics to measure success.

• Leverage data and insights to continuously refine change strategies and improve outcomes.

Capability Building & Enablement

• Design and deliver training that supports not just knowledge transfer, but behavioral and mindset shifts.

• Coach managers and teams to effectively lead and sustain change.

• 10+ years of experience leading organizational change, culture transformation, or process adoption initiatives.
• Proven ability to drive behavior change and embed new ways of working in complex, cross-functional environments.
• Experience partnering with senior leadership to influence culture, alignment, and decision-making.
• Strong understanding of change management methodologies (e.g., PROSCI, ACMP), with ability to apply them pragmatically.
• Exceptional communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence across all levels of the organization.
• Experience designing and measuring adoption and culture-related success metrics.
• Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Communications, Organizational Development, Education).

jobs.title: Human Resources Business Partner
jobs.description:
Reporting to the HRBP Manager, Ventures, the Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP) at Alarm.com will serve as a trusted partner to leaders and employees on a wide range of people-related matters. This remote position is based in Texas and will support HR initiatives, employee experience, and organizational effectiveness across several subsidiary companies within the Alarm.com family.

This role supports key areas including performance management, employee relations, talent development, leadership coaching, recruiting support, workforce planning, and compliance with applicable employment and OSHA requirements. The HRBP will play an important role in supporting a varied employee population throughout the full employee lifecycle and helping foster a positive and high-performing workplace culture as the company scales.

Responsibilities

• Serve as a strategic HR partner by providing tailored guidance, coaching, and support to leaders and employees across the organization.

• Build strong, trusted relationships throughout the organization to understand business priorities, team dynamics, and operational challenges.

• Support organizational change initiatives by helping leaders and teams navigate transitions effectively and thoughtfully.

• Provide HR expertise and guidance in areas including performance management, employee relations, talent development, leadership coaching, workforce planning, and OSHA-related compliance requirements.

• Partner with leaders to promote and maintain compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws and workplace safety regulations, including OSHA standards.

• Proactively identify team and leadership development opportunities and recommend practical, scalable solutions.

• Guide managers through employee relations matters with professionalism, consistency, and sound judgment.

• Collaborate with Recruiting, Learning & Development, Compensation, HR Operations, and other cross-functional partners to deliver effective HR solutions and programs.
