jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technical Excellence & Escalations
jobs.location: US - Hybrid - Massachusetts - Boston , US - Headquarters - Maryland - Columbia
jobs.description:
Who is Tenable?

Tenable® is the Exposure Management company. Over 40,000 organizations around the globe rely on Tenable to understand and reduce cyber risk. Our global employees support 65 percent of the Fortune 500, 50 percent of the Global 2000, and large government agencies. Come be part of our journey!

What makes Tenable such a great place to work?

Ask a member of our team and they’ll answer, “Our people!” We work together to build and innovate best-in-class cybersecurity solutions for our customers; all while creating a culture of belonging, respect, and excellence where we can be our best selves. When you’re part of our #OneTenable team, you can expect to partner with some of the most talented and passionate people in the industry, and have the support and resources you need to do work that truly matters. We deliver results that exceed expectations and we win together!

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. without sponsorship. We are unable to provide sponsorship for work visas of any kind at the time of hire, or at any point during employment. This includes, but is not limited to: F1-OPT, F1-CPT, H-1B, TN, J-1, etc

Your Role:

The Senior Manager, Technical Excellence & Escalations leads the two teams that sit between Technical Support and the rest of the business: the global Technical Excellence team, staffed by our Technical Leads, and the global Escalations Engineering team.

Both produce Tenable's earliest and clearest signal about product supportability and customer risk. Both have historically produced that signal faster than the organization could act on it. This role exists to close that gap.

This is not a queue-management job. The Senior Manager is accountable for two outcomes: turning Technical Lead expertise and escalation findings into tracked change with Product and Engineering, and running one escalations practice that behaves identically in AMER, EMEA, and APJ.

The role sits within Operations & Scale and works in close partnership with the Sr. Director, who sets overall strategy and carries the executive narrative. The Senior Manager owns the operating model, the day-to-day practice, and the working-level relationships with Product and Engineering that make change actually happen. They lead senior individual contributors who are already force multipliers — which makes this a job about influence and orchestration, not direction.

Who You Are:

• An orchestrator, not a bottleneck. You create the conditions for senior experts to influence the organization instead of routing their work through yourself.

• Technically credible. You have the depth to earn respect from Principal-level engineers and to challenge an Engineering assessment that doesn't hold up.

• A clear communicator under pressure. You can hold a room containing both a frustrated customer and an Engineering lead, and translate technical detail into business consequence.

• A systems thinker. You are drawn to the pattern behind the escalation. You would rather fix the class of problem than win the individual case.

• Comfortable influencing without authority. Much of what this role must accomplish depends on teams you don't own.

• Effective remotely. You build trust and hold a team together without relying on being in the room, and you communicate in writing well enough that distance isn't a handicap.

• A developer of senior talent. You are energized by growing people who are already very good, and you give direct feedback.

Your Opportunity:

Technical Excellence Team

• Run the operating model and product coverage plan for the global Technical Excellence team — every strategic product has clear lead ownership, defined authority, and no coverage gaps across theaters.

• Set the team's working agenda: what leads work on, what they own, and how their time splits between reactive escalation support and proactive supportability work.

• Turn Technical Lead findings — defect patterns, supportability gaps, documentation failures, recurring friction — into one prioritized, evidence-backed agenda, not a stream of individual product complaints.

• Position Technical Leads as credible partners in Product and Engineering forums, with the data, framing, and support they need to influence rather than escalate.

• Contribute to the Technical Lead career path with the Education & Enablement Manager, and apply it consistently — progression from Technical Lead through Senior and Principal, and the competencies that separate each grade.

Global Escalations Practice

• Own the global escalations practice day to day: process design, entry and exit criteria, severity definitions, roles, communication standards, and adherence.

• Drive it to a single global standard. One model, consistently applied and measured across all theaters, with regional variance only where legally or operationally required.

• Operate and enforce the working agreement with Product Engineering — SLA adherence for escalated defects, prioritization criteria, update cadence, and follow-through on resolution commitments. Escalate structural breakdowns to the Sr. Director.

• Own the quality of post-escalation output. Every RCA and post-incident report produces a tracked action, not a filed document.

• Build the prevention agenda: analyze root cause patterns and drive the upstream product, process, tooling, or enablement changes that reduce escalation volume and re-escalation rate.

• Act as the Technical Support point of contact for high-severity customer situations — providing assurance and coordination without displacing the assigned Escalations Engineer.

Driving Change Across the Organization

• Represent Technical Support in roadmap, release readiness, and quality forums at the Product Management and Engineering Manager level, making the supportability and escalation-risk case with data.

• Run the working-level feedback loop into Product and Engineering: defined cadence, shared prioritization, visible tracking from support signal to shipped change.

• Assemble the evidence behind supportability investment — ticket volume, escalation cost, re-escalation overhead — and partner with the Sr. Director to convert it into a business case that earns engineering capacity.

• Partner with Engineering on release quality gates so Technical Support has meaningful input before GA, not remediation duty after it.

• Represent both teams in cross-functional work with Customer Success, Sales Engineering, and Professional Services where escalation or account risk is in scope.

• Produce the regular supportability and escalation readout for the Sr. Director: narrative, trend, and recommendation — not raw metrics. Present directly to senior leadership as requested.

• Work with the Operations Manager to instrument escalation and Technical Lead activity in TSO reporting, so the teams' signal is visible without manual pulls.

Leadership & People Development

• Lead and develop a senior, highly autonomous, globally distributed team, including the Principal Technical Lead as a technical partner and strategic extension of the function.

• Operate as a player-coach: hold the operating cadence and coach the team, and step personally into a live critical escalation or a difficult Engineering conversation when it matters.

• Build succession depth in both teams and eliminate single-person dependency on strategic products and accounts.

• Partner with the Education & Enablement Manager — a peer in the same function — to close skill gaps in both populations and feed field learnings into broader Technical Support enablement and certification.

• Set goals, performance expectations, and measurement for both teams in line with global Technical Support objectives.

• Drive AI adoption within Technical Lead and Escalations workflows under the Support AI governance framework, acting as the proving ground for capability the wider TSO will inherit.

What You'll Need:

• 8+ years in Technical Support, Escalation Management, or customer-facing engineering in enterprise software, with recent focus on security or vulnerability management.

• 3+ years managing technical teams — ideally senior individual contributors, technical leads, or escalation engineers. Experience managing remote and globally distributed teams strongly preferred.

• Hands-on experience running an escalation practice or program, including process design and cross-functional coordination.

• Demonstrated ability to influence product and engineering priorities using support and escalation data.

• Experience operating within Support–Engineering agreements, including SLA adherence for defect resolution.

• Comfort with support metrics and the analysis behind them — escalation volume, re-escalation rate, time-to-resolution, ticket volume reduction — and the ability to build the evidence case for investment.

• Strong understanding of Tenable's product portfolio and security best practices, or the demonstrated ability to reach it quickly.

• Technical foundation across networking, authentication, operating systems, and cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) sufficient to lead technical discussions credibly.

• Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable with senior stakeholders and with customers at any level.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or equivalent experience.

• Able to work in a hybrid/on-site capacity at our office in Columbia MD or Boston MA.

• Available to provide leadership coverage for critical escalations outside standard business hours as needed, and to work across AMER, EMEA, and APJ time zones to support globally distributed teams.

• Occasional travel as required for team, customer, and cross-functional engagements.

• Flexibility to perform other duties as deemed necessary by management.

And Ideally:

• Cybersecurity or adjacent enterprise security SaaS experience.

• Prior time as a Technical Lead, Principal Engineer, or Escalations Engineer — credibility earned in the seat.

• Product Management or program management exposure.

• Familiarity with AI-assisted support workflows and their governance.

• Experience supporting FedRAMP or other regulated environments.

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Flight Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Spacecraft Flight Software Engineer is responsible for determining how our spacecraft behaves and operates in orbit and building reliable software to ensure it happens. The team is responsible for all phases of development, starting from requirements capture through testing and flight operational support.

Responsibilities

• Develop reliable flight software that determine how the spacecraft, satellite bus, and reentry capsule operate throughout the entire mission.

• Write quality structured bare metal, RTOS, or Linux based software for embedded processors in C++.

• Own all aspects of software development, from design, testing, and integration.

• Scope projects including requirements capture and initial design trades given open-ended problems.

• Ensure system quality and performance through software test, verification, and validation (V&V) technique.

• Teamwork, communicate and problem solve in a collaborative environment.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, math, physics, engineering or equivalent technical experience in safety critical software.

• 5+ years of experience in the development of spacecraft or similar safety critical software.

• Experience with development in C++, along with a strong understanding of the language concepts.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• End-to-end experience building and launching a spacecraft.

• Experience developing and testing real-time embedded systems.

• Experience with safety-critical software, especially for aerospace applications.

• Experience with CCSDS telemetry and telecommand system.

• Experience with F' or cFS framework.

• Experience with Python, or Rust.

• Knowledge of basic analog and digital electronics.

• Familiarity with SPI, I2C, CAN, EtherCAT.

Pay Range

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA.

Workplace Experience & Perks

jobs.title: Senior Director, 340B Strategy
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Senior Director of 340B Strategy partners with health systems to enhance, optimize, and transform their 340B programs through a combination of strategic advisory services, operational excellence, data-driven insights, and innovative technology solutions. The role is responsible for identifying and implementing strategies that enhance 340B savings, improve program performance, strengthen compliance, and expand access to care for vulnerable patient populations.

As a senior leader, the Senior Director serves as a trusted advisor to health system pharmacy, finance, compliance, operations, and executive leadership teams, helping organizations navigate the evolving 340B landscape while developing sustainable strategies to achieve both financial and patient care objectives. This role is at the forefront of advancing 340B programs nationwide through innovative problem-solving, emerging technologies, and continuous program optimization.

The Senior Director is accountable for the full lifecycle of Shields' 340B services across their assigned portfolio. This includes program assessments, strategic planning, implementation of new initiatives, operational optimization, technology deployment, regulatory guidance, and ongoing advisory support. The role works closely with internal operations leadership and health system partners to identify opportunities for growth, enhance program capture and savings, implement enhancement strategies, optimize contract pharmacy, evaluate new 340B opportunities, and leverage technology to improve visibility and program performance.

The Senior Director is expected to act as a subject matter expert and thought leader on all aspects of 340B strategy, operations, compliance, reimbursement, and emerging industry developments. Success in this role is measured by the ability to deliver meaningful financial and operational outcomes, strengthen partner relationships, and drive continued innovation across the 340B ecosystem.

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

The following duties are representative of the essential functions of this position. Additional responsibilities may be assigned as business needs require.

• Serve as the thought leader on all 340B matters with credible experience working with and influencing pharmacy, finance, and operations teams across health systems.

• Develop and drive 340B strategy across the regions, continuing to evolve 340B strategies based on the 340B Federal statute, HRSA guidelines, HRSA audit trends, and industry knowledge.

• Maintain a thorough understanding of the 340B program, including monitoring legislative changes or proposed 340B regulations, and communicate current 340B trends and interpretations directly affecting health system partners.

• Analyze 340B opportunities across the regions, including contract pharmacy expansion opportunities.

• Develop customized roadmaps and granular project plans for executing 340B enhancement strategies across the regions and project manage to completion.

• Drive the implementation and track execution of 340B strategies across health system partners.

• Develop annual 340B strategy targets and guide health systems through the implementation of 340B strategies to increase the number of 340B eligible patients and drive 340B savings. This includes but is not limited to provider-based clinic conversions and implementation of Collaborative Drug Therapy Management programs.

• Project manage provider-based clinic conversions and implementation of Collaborative Drug Therapy Management programs.

• Perform weekly audits of non-340B prescriptions dispensed by partner pharmacy locations and analyze for missed opportunities. This includes gathering supporting documentation from the EMR to identify 340B optimization opportunities.

• Develop an innate knowledge of partner pharmacy dispensing systems, EMRs, and various 340B platforms to monitor 340B activity.

• Implement 340B programs for new pharmacies, including advising on 340B TPA and accumulator setup.

• Review Hospital Medicare Cost Reports and identify 340B-eligible departments for opportunities.

• Develop and/or update 340B policies and procedures utilized by health system partners to reflect 340B program best practices.

• Develop and update 340B program reporting detailing 340B volume, financial value, and other 340B KPIs as needed.

Required Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience

Experience

• Six or more years of direct 340B program management or 340B consulting experience

Technical Skills

• Proficient in Excel and PowerPoint

Additional Qualifications

• Entrepreneurial attitude with a willingness to roll up sleeves, work alongside team members, and create value quickly

• Highly motivated, results-driven professional who thrives in a team-oriented environment

• Outstanding leadership skills with the ability to lead regional 340B teams, motivate team members, and serve as the subject matter expert for health system counterparts

• Exceptional analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interface effectively with staff, physicians, patients, executives, and colleagues at all levels

• Strong technical aptitude and ability to navigate medication management software, healthcare billing systems, electronic medical records, 340B third-party administrators, pharmacy management and dispensing systems, and Microsoft applications

• Ability to take a data-driven approach and distill complex subjects into structured frameworks and actionable plans

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with 340B TPA systems

• Exposure to 340B from covered entity, pharmacy, and TPA perspectives

Work Environment

• Remote work environment

• Travel to health system partners, corporate offices, and conferences as needed

Travel Requirements

• Up to 20% travel required

Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

Job Overview

As an Operations Automation Specialist, you will personally resolve provider inquiries — and then build the tools that make resolving them one-by-one unnecessary.

Today, resolving a provider's question well requires detailed manual auditing and review across multiple systems. It's careful work, and it doesn't scale. The data needed to answer these questions faster and more accurately already exists across our data sources — and modern AI tools give us the opportunity to bring that work together and scale it in a way we haven't yet.

You'll start by doing the job as it exists today: working real provider inquiries, learning the systems, and building the judgment that comes from firsthand experience with the problem. From there, your job shifts toward building — using AI-assisted workflows to resolve inquiries faster, surface patterns worth fixing at the root, and move providers toward getting their answers without needing to contact us at all. This is a new kind of role for Lantern, built specifically because this problem is ready for it.

This is a technical role in the lowercase-t sense: you don't need to arrive as a software engineer, and this isn't the data-analyst track either — it's for people with the instinct to spot patterns and automate them away, even without the formal technical background yet to do it at scale. For the right person, it's a deliberate stepping stone toward more technical roles at Lantern over time.

We're deliberately not writing this as a data-engineering job. Someone who already codes fluently can thrive here, but so can a business-minded person with real communication skills and the drive to build — the second profile is just as much the target as the first.

We're not narrowing this to one experience level. A recent grad with the right instincts is a big part of who we want in the pipeline — but so is someone with five or ten years of practical business experience who has been deliberately building toward exactly this kind of role. More time doing the work often means sharper pattern recognition, not a worse fit. We'll teach you the domain — you don't need to know claims or healthcare going in. What we won't do is teach you SQL or Claude Code step by step; the expectation is that you go figure new tools out largely on your own, the same way people have always picked up new tools on the job.

What You'll Do:

Resolve, hands-on

• Work a live queue of provider claims inquiries — status, payment amount, denial and rejection questions, aged-claim batches — through to accurate resolution

• Audit individual claims across systems to confirm they were submitted, validated, priced, and paid correctly

• Escalate genuine pricing or appeals determinations, and document what you learn so the pattern can eventually be automated

Understand the problem at scale

• Query claims, pricing, and provider data directly using SQL — you'll pick up our specific tools (including Databricks) on the job — to characterize inquiry volume, root causes, and cost to serve — much of which isn't measured today

• Separate inquiries caused by real payment problems from inquiries caused by providers simply lacking visibility — they need different fixes

Build the fix

• Design and build AI-assisted workflows that triage inquiries, retrieve the relevant claim and contract facts, validate payments, and draft accurate, provider-ready responses

• Build in verification, not just automation — a confident wrong answer about a payment amount is worse than a slower correct one

• Test against real ticket volume, measure impact honestly, and iterate

Push upstream

• Where a category of inquiry traces back to a fixable upstream issue — deferred claims, ingestion errors, notification gaps — work the root cause, not just the symptom

• Contribute to provider self-service so fewer questions need to reach us in the first place

About You:

We're looking for someone with the business and communication fundamentals to do this job well today, plus the eagerness to build the automation that makes it unnecessary tomorrow. This is not a data-engineering posting — a business background, a support/ops background, or a fresh grad with the right instincts can all be a great fit, provided the willingness to learn is real.

Core

• You can communicate clearly and confidently with providers and internal stakeholders — you can pick up the phone, have a real conversation, and explain what's happening in plain terms, not just write it up

• You have (or can quickly build) a working understanding of the business and financial side of how claims and payments move — you're not purely a technical person who can't connect the dots to what the business needs

• You have a genuine desire to expand your SQL skills and to use Python and AI tools — including agentic coding tools like Claude Code — to improve how work gets done, even if you're not there yet; you'd rather build something than just talk about it

• You think carefully about correctness: your instinct is to ask “how would I know if this were wrong,” and then build the check

• You're comfortable in ambiguity, in an environment where the documentation is thin and the systems don't always agree with each other

• You start by actually doing the resolution work — the same work our team does well every day — because you can't build good automation for a process you haven't done yourself; understanding it that closely is what makes the eventual automation worth trusting

Strongly preferred

• Hands-on SQL and/or Python experience, and real fluency with modern AI tools — including agentic coding tools like Claude Code — with something you've actually built with them to show for it

• A year or more of work experience — internship, part-time, or full-time — especially something that required real conversations with people (customers, providers, clients)

• Background or coursework in process improvement — comfortable getting into how a workflow actually operates today, spotting where it breaks, and proposing a fix

• A business, finance, economics, or business-intelligence academic background — these programs tend to build in real SQL (and often some Python and AI-tool) exposure alongside the communication and financial-literacy skills this role needs

• Exposure to revenue cycle, claims, payer operations, or provider billing — deep expertise isn't required, we'll teach the domain, but prior contact with how claims get paid shortens the ramp meaningfully

• Experience in a support, service, or operations function, with an instinct for what the person on the other end actually needs

Not required

• A formal software engineering background or computer science degree — you're not building distributed systems, you're using tools that already exist to make an operational process dramatically better

• Already being an expert in SQL, Python, or AI tooling — what we're looking for is real curiosity and a track record of teaching yourself new tools; we'll give you real problems, context, and room to grow into them, not a step-by-step curriculum

• Hands-on experience with Databricks or other enterprise data-engineering tooling — that's specific to our internal stack, and you'll pick it up here with real access and context once you're on the team

• Any specific number of years of "AI experience" — the tools are too new for that bar to mean anything yet; genuine, demonstrated use matters, not tenure

What Success Looks Like

At 3 months: You're resolving provider inquiries independently, including complex ones. The inquiry population is measured and segmented for the first time. At least one AI-assisted workflow is live and measurably cutting down manual handling.

At 6 months: A growing share of provider inquiries are resolved without a manual research step. Cost per resolved inquiry is down, resolutions per person are up, and more providers are getting answers without needing to contact us at all.

Location & Logistics

Hybrid | Dallas, TX or New York, NY | 3 days per week in office (required due to the sensitivity of the data this role handles)

Lantern does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other reason prohibited by law in the provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

About You:

• INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.

• You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.

• You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.

• Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.

• You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern.

jobs.title: Director Touring
jobs.description:
Company Information
For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer.

Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations.

If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer!

Position Summary

The primary responsibilities of the Touring Director are to drive touring revenue through owned, co-promoted, and strategic touring opportunities while leading the development and execution of CMN's touring strategy. This role is responsible for identifying and securing content, evaluating market opportunities, and determining where, when, and how the company strategically assumes risk to maximize revenue and profitability. The Touring Director builds and maintains long-term relationships with artists, agents, promoters, venues, and industry partners to expand touring opportunities and strengthen CMN's market position. This role exercises substantial independent judgment and discretion in evaluating investments, negotiating touring opportunities, developing market strategies, and allocating resources to achieve business objectives. Additionally, the Touring Director ensures a seamless transition of confirmed tours and shows to Touring Managers for execution and delivery.

Primary Job Responsibilities:

• Drive touring revenue through owned, co-promoted, and strategic touring opportunities.

• Lead the development and execution of touring strategies that support company growth and profitability objectives.

• Identify, evaluate, and secure touring content, artist partnerships, and market opportunities.

• Assess financial, operational, and market risks associated with touring opportunities and recommend investment strategies.

• Determine where, when, and how the company assumes risk on touring, co-promotion, and event opportunities.

• Develop and execute market expansion strategies to increase touring revenue and strengthen CMN's presence in key markets.

• Negotiate tour agreements, co-promotion deals, artist agreements, venue agreements, and other business arrangements.

• Build and maintain strategic relationships with artists, agents, managers, promoters, venues, and industry stakeholders.

• Evaluate market trends, consumer demand, competitive activity, and industry developments to inform business decisions.

• Analyze tour performance, profitability, and revenue opportunities and make recommendations to maximize returns.

• Collaborate with Booking Agents, Artist Management, Marketing, Finance, Production, and Operations teams to ensure alignment on touring initiatives.

• Develop tour budgets, revenue forecasts, and financial models to support business planning and decision-making.

• Represent the company at industry conferences, showcases, meetings, and networking events.

• Identify and pursue new business opportunities, partnerships, and revenue streams within the touring and live entertainment sectors.

• Present strategic recommendations, business cases, and performance analyses to senior leadership.

• Transition confirmed tours and shows to Touring Managers and Operations teams for execution and delivery.

• Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned that are consistent with the nature and level of the position.

What You Bring to the Table:

• Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Entertainment Management, Music Business, Marketing, Finance, or a related field; equivalent industry experience may be considered.

• Minimum of 5 years of experience in touring, concert promotion, live entertainment, talent buying, event production, artist management, or related industry roles.

• Proven track record of generating revenue and managing profitable touring, promotion, or live entertainment initiatives.

• Demonstrated experience evaluating business opportunities, financial risk, and market expansion strategies.

• Experience negotiating artist agreements, tour agreements, co-promotion deals, venue agreements, and related contracts.

• Strong understanding of the live entertainment, touring, concert promotion, and venue industries.

• Established network of industry contacts, including artists, agents, managers, promoters, venues, and business partners.

• Demonstrated success developing strategic partnerships and long-term business relationships.

• Strong financial acumen with experience developing budgets, forecasts, profitability analyses, and business plans.

• Exceptional negotiation, business development, and relationship management skills.

• Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and decision-making capabilities.

• Ability to evaluate risk and make informed business decisions that impact revenue, profitability, and company growth.

• Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, CRM platforms, and financial reporting tools.

• Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and lead cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced environment.

• Knowledge of current industry trends, touring economics, market conditions, and emerging opportunities.

• Fluency in both English and Spanish (written and verbal) is required.

• Ability to travel domestically and internationally and work evenings, weekends, and holidays as business needs require.

• Ability to exercise independent judgment and discretion in evaluating touring opportunities, negotiating business agreements, managing financial risk, and making strategic decisions that impact company performance.

Payscale: $90k-$110K

Bonus: This position is eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Benefits: Full-time: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: medical, dental and vision insurance, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, company paid basic life insurance, voluntary life insurance, parental leave, 401k Plan (with a current employer match of 3%), flexible spending and health savings account options, and wellness offerings.

AEG reserves the right to change or modify the employee’s job description whether orally or in writing, at any time during the employment relationship.  AEG may require an employee to perform duties outside their normal description.

AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants, and we comply with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws in making hiring and employee decisions.  We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, marital status, disability, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected status recognized by applicable federal, state or local law.

jobs.description:
**Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or U.S. Permanent Residents (Green Card holders) to meet customer and regulatory requirements**

Who We Are

We are pioneering modular motion technologies to power the next generation of innovation for Industrial, Aerospace and Defense. If you're excited about disrupting legacy industries, and passionate about motor control technology, let's chat!

We are at the forefront of innovation, crafting exclusive motion control components that propel the industrial, aerospace, and defense sectors into the future.

A couple other things:

• We are open to relocating you

• We have great benefits

• We are well funded, and already generating revenue

• We are located in beautiful Torrance, CA and just moved into a new large hangar facility

What you'll do:

We are seeking a versatile, high-impact Engineer to lead the development of mission-critical hardware. This is a "full-lifecycle" role where you will own everything from the initial conversion of ambiguous concepts into rigorous requirements to the hands-on assembly and environmental qualification of flight hardware.

• Requirements Architecture: Translate high-level, ambiguous mission needs into actionable functional and operational requirements for complex electromechanical systems.

• Precision Mechanism Design: Design and iterate on electromagnetic actuators and intricate mechanisms, integrating components such as precision gears, bearings, lead screws, braking systems, and encoders.

• Ruggedized Avionics: Develop high-performance avionics enclosures, focusing on innovative thermal management (heat rejection) and structural survivability in extreme, high-vibration, or vacuum environments.

• Environmental Qualification: Architect the test equipment and methodologies required for formal hardware qualification, ensuring total compliance with DO-160 and MIL-STD-810 standards.

• Cross-Functional Leadership: Act as a technical anchor across the organization, guiding integration efforts and supporting multidisciplinary teams through complex system testing.

• Supply Chain & Quality Advocacy: Partner closely with external suppliers to ensure the delivery of conforming hardware; proactively manage manufacturing deviations to maintain rigorous quality and schedule standards.

• Hands-on Execution: Maintain a "design-build-test" mindset, taking personal responsibility for the assembly, bring-up, and debugging of your own hardware prototypes.

What you need:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

• Experience: 5+ years of experience through the full product lifecycle—from initial ideation and prototyping to high-fidelity production.

• Technical Expertise: A deep intuition for electromagnetic principles and a mastery of mechanical load paths and load cases.

• Analysis & Simulation: Proficiency in sizing analysis for strength, fatigue, and life cycles of actuator components (gears, shafts, housings).

• CAD Mastery: Advanced design experience in SolidWorks (or equivalent 3D modeling packages), including complex assemblies and configuration management.

• Manufacturing & GD&T: Fluency in ASME Y14.5 GD&T standards; ability to produce high-quality 2D drawings and collaborate with vendors to solve DFM (Design for Manufacturing) hurdles.

• Standards & Qualification: Proven track record of qualifying hardware against rigorous aerospace or military standards (DO-160, MIL-STD-810).

• Grit: A "builder" mindset—you are as comfortable at a computer as you are in the lab spinning wrenches and debugging your own hardware.

Nice to have:

• Qualification: Experience designing custom test equipment, writing formal procedures, and executing complex qualification test campaigns.

• Gearbox Specialization: Detailed knowledge of AGMA Standards, gearbox design analysis (ratios, backlash, lubrication), and specialized fabrication methods.

• Process Versatility: Experience navigating both high-compliance, "heavy" programs and fast-paced, lean R&D environments.

What we have to offer:

We are not just building components. We are reshaping the future of the Aerospace and Defense component industry, which is a $300B+ market! Come join us and help build next generation systems that will make a massive impact at global scale.

• We offer competitive compensation: $160,000 to $190,000 base salary + equity

• Exceptional healthcare benefits, Medical is 100% covered by the company

• Flexible PTO

• 401K

• More to come!

jobs.title: Account Partner, Enterprise (UK)
jobs.description:
Do you want to empower organizations to build smarter compensation strategies while ensuring fair pay for all employees?

Syndio is the leading pay governance and compensation intelligence platform. We help organizations make better pay decisions at every stage of the compensation lifecycle, from leveling and offers to promotions and merit. Our platform gives HR, compensation, and finance leaders the data and decision support they need to govern pay fairly, compliantly, and with confidence. We partner with many of the world’s most recognized and respected enterprises, helping them implement leading-edge compensation solutions with expert guidance and analyzing pay for over 10 million employees across the world.

Join us in our mission to help companies make smarter pay decisions they can trust!

About the role

As an Account Partner, you will own the full client relationship across a book of enterprise accounts headquartered in the UK and EU, many operating across multiple EU member states that are serious about transforming the future of pay. You are the person who makes the Syndio commercial motion real: driving adoption, expanding the Syndio platform, and running a book where every renewal is earned long before it’s negotiated. In Europe, the EU Pay Transparency Directive means our customers need Syndio to work in practice, not just on paper. You'll guide their teams through the platform so they get full value from what they own, supported by our in-house domain experts and Syndi on the regulatory elements.

Most companies see the EU Pay Transparency Directive as a reporting problem. You'll help them see it as a pay governance problem. Every pay gap starts as a decision made without the right information, and Syndio governs those decisions as they're made, not a year later when they have to be explained.

Why this job is exciting

You're the person customers call when their CHRO needs board-ready analysis, when an employee submits their first right-to-information request, or the first pay gap reporting cycle is approaching, when a works council asks how pay decisions are being made, and most importantly, when they're ready to transform how they make pay decisions across the org. You anticipate those calls before they come, arriving with a point of view on where each account’s compliance posture is heading and what to do about it before leadership asks. Your customers trust you because you understand their business, not just the product.

Building that trust is how you build a commercial relationship. You earn executive alignment with the office of the CHRO and CFO by being the advisor who helps your customers think through hard problems, not the person who manages their contract. That advisory credibility is what opens the path from compliance-only into governance at scale, and what makes renewals a confirmation of partnership rather than a negotiation.

About you

• 5+ years of enterprise selling experience — Account Management, Enterprise Account Executive, or equivalent GTM roles in B2B SaaS across the UK and Europe, where you personally owned GRR and NRR. Proven expansion and retention wins in a complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise environment, with quantified results you can speak to clearly.

• You drive adoption hands-on. You're comfortable running platform walkthroughs and enablement sessions, helping customers get their data into good shape, and showing them how to use RTI responses, readiness reporting and gap budgeting day to day. You track usage and turn it into the renewal story.

• You are a self-starter when it comes to delivering value and know how to activate an expansion strategy within an account with a large stakeholder group.

• Your customers think of you as an advisor first — the person who helps them think through hard problems — and a commercial owner second. You have relationships and a track record to prove it.

• You understand your customers’ business objectives. You have working knowledge of the EU Pay Transparency Directive and what it asks of employers. You spot when a customer needs deeper regulatory support and bring in the right expert, rather than trying to be one.

• You earn CHRO access by building VP and Director-level alignment — across HR, Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Legal, and Finance. You understand each stakeholder’s lens, build the internal consensus that gets you into the room that matters, and know that CHRO sponsorship is what unlocks multi-product expansion.

• You own GRR, NRR and quota end to end: renewals first, then expansion and pipeline. You run a disciplined book: you know how to allocate time for prospecting within client accounts and know where to focus for retention and expansion. You work these accounts early, and you hit your number consistently. Your track record proves it.

• You’re an effective orchestrator of internal resources — you know when to pull in cross-functional teammates and executives to advance an opportunity and how to keep commercial ownership through the close and build category-defining partnerships.

• You're organised enough to run a book across several countries, time zones and procurement processes without renewals slipping.

• Working proficiency in a second European language (French or German especially)

Nice to have

• Background in Tech or enterprise SaaS, selling into an HR or Finance buyer.

• Experience selling AI-native platforms with an expanding product roadmap — you know how to drive adoption of what exists today and build customer conviction around a platform that compounds value over time.

• Experience expanding a customer from one product into a second within a platform.

• Consulting background or experience in project management is a plus.

• Energized by building. You’re drawn to companies defining a new category, not ones running a mature playbook.

• You have a solid working command of compensation and/or decision intelligence — enough to have a credible, thought-provoking conversation with the office of the CHRO or CFO about what it means to govern pay decisions at scale through technology.

Why you'll love it here:

• 💰 Competitive Compensation. For this role our salary is targeted at £75,000-83,500 base salary / 150,000-167,000 OTE. Final offer amounts are determined by factors such as experience and expertise.

• 🏆 Syndio Equity. So you can share in Syndio’s success.

• 🏝 25 days PTO, plus paid sick & safe time, compassion leave, and voting leave.

• 🏥 Private Medical Insurance including dental, optical and mental health support.

• 💊 Health Cash Plan to claim back everyday costs like dental, optical and physio.

• 🛡️ Life Assurance, Income Protection & Critical Illness Cover.

• 🏦 Workplace Pension. To help you save for your future.

• 📍 Remote within the UK #LI-Remote

The interview overview

Below you'll find an outline of the interview plan for our Account Partner position. Please note that this is what we expect the process to look like; we may ask you for supplemental information or require an additional step before making a final decision.

• 30 min interview with a member of our Talent Team

ServiceNow is looking for a Senior Staff Product Manager to lead the conversational core of its Voice AI platform. jobs.title: International Field Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sieve is a multimodal lab curating the world’s highest-quality training datasets, spanning video, audio, images, text, and 3D. We combine exabyte-scale data infrastructure with novel multimodal understanding techniques to push the frontier of foundation models. We exist to solve one of the biggest bottlenecks in AI: high-quality training data.

We partner with top AI labs and did $XXM last quarter alone, with a team of roughly 40 people. We raised our Series A from firms including Matrix Partners, Swift Ventures, Y Combinator, and AI Grant.




WHY NOW

We’re standing up data operations internationally — recording footage, hiring people on the ground, and building the local capacity those programs need. That work won’t scale from SF alone. We need someone who’s done on-the-ground ops and can expand teams internationally without waiting for a perfect playbook.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring an International Field Operations Lead to help build and expand Sieve’s on-the-ground operations abroad. You’ll help set up local collection (including recording footage), hire and manage people in-market, and turn early international efforts into reliable operating systems.

This is a hands-on ops role for someone with direct field experience — not a remote-only coordinator. You’ll travel when needed, solve problems in the moment, and build the teams and processes that make international data collection repeatable.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Stand up international ops: Help launch and expand on-the-ground operations in priority markets, including footage recording and related collection workflows.

 - Hire and grow local teams: Source, hire, onboard, and manage people in-market; build the staffing model as volume grows.

 - Own day-to-day field execution: Solve logistics, quality, scheduling, and vendor/partner issues so collection stays on track.

 - Build repeatable playbooks: Turn one-off market launches into documented processes for hiring, training, quality control, and escalation.

 - Partner with SF product and ops: Translate project requirements into field plans; feed back what’s working and what breaks in-market.

 - Scale carefully: Balance speed with quality, compliance, and contributor/operator experience as we expand.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Live international ops that reliably deliver footage and other required data

 - Local teams hired, trained, and producing without constant firefighting from SF

 - Clear playbooks for launching and expanding into new markets

 - Improving quality, throughput, and time-to-launch across sites

 - Strong coordination between field teams and SF stakeholders


REQUIREMENTS

 - Direct on-the-ground operations experience, ideally expanding teams internationally

 - Track record hiring and managing people in the field (contractors, vendors, or full-time)

 - Comfort with ambiguity, travel, and building systems where none exist yet

 - Strong operator instincts: logistics, quality, people management, and follow-through

 - Clear communicator across time zones and cultures

 - Based in San Francisco or willing to relocate; able to travel internationally as needed


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in data collection, media production, field research, marketplace ops, or logistics in emerging markets

 - Prior work standing up ops in multiple countries

 - Familiarity with physical AI, robotics, or AI training data workflows

 - Language skills relevant to priority markets


BENEFITS

 - 401(k) and full health insurance

 - Breakfast, lunch, and dinner covered, plus your choice of snacks

 - Ubers covered home



*All roles at Sieve require you to be onsite in San Francisco 5 days per week

jobs.title: Senior Information Security Architect
jobs.description:
Verisign helps enable the security, stability, and resiliency of the internet. We are a trusted provider of internet infrastructure services for the networked world and deliver unmatched performance in domain name system (DNS) services.

We are a mission focused, values driven company where each individual can contribute to building a stronger, more secure internet.  We offer a dynamic and flexible work environment with competitive benefits and the ability to grow your career.

The mission of the Security Architecture Team is to define and advance secure, resilient architecture across Verisign’s systems, networks, applications, cloud platforms, data environments, and emerging technologies. The team combines deep technical expertise with enterprise strategy to reduce risk, enable innovation, and establish security patterns that scale across the organization.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Information Security Architect. This senior individual-contributor role shapes enterprise security strategy, reference architectures, standards, and technical requirements across the entire company. The architect will lead high-impact design decisions, resolve complex cross-domain security challenges, and advise engineering and executive leaders on risk, tradeoffs, and long-term technology direction.

Working across security engineering, infrastructure, application development, cloud, data, and AI teams, this role ensures security is built into critical services from concept through implementation in production. The Senior Information Security Architect will authoritatively guide the defense of a diverse hybrid technology ecosystem - safeguarding mission essential on-premises architecture, modern cloud platforms, secure application pipelines, and emerging enterprise AI workloads.

Key Responsibilities

• Define enterprise security architecture strategy, principles, reference architectures, reusable patterns, and multi-year roadmaps across network, endpoint, identity, application, cloud, container, data, and detection and response domains

• Lead security architecture engagement for complex, high-risk, and cross-functional programs; translate business objectives, threat intelligence, and risk appetite into scalable technical controls and design requirements

• Establish architecture and security requirements for AI/ML systems, including secure MLOps, model and data lifecycle protection, identity and authorization, platform isolation, model provenance, monitoring, privacy, and responsible-use guardrails

• Review generative and agentic AI designs—including retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, third-party models, APIs, plugins, tools, and autonomous actions—and address controls to mitigate the risks of prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agency, insecure output handling, and AI supply-chain compromise

• Perform threat modeling, architecture reviews, and security design assessments for critical systems and emerging technologies; document risk decisions and guide remediation or compensating controls

• Identify systemic gaps in the security posture, develop prioritized recommendations and investment roadmaps, and communicate technical risk and tradeoffs clearly to executive leadership

• Evaluate security technologies and vendors, guide proofs of concept, and ensure proposed solutions are interoperable, supportable, measurable, and aligned with strategic architecture

Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience

• 10+ years of broad information security experience, including significant experience with security architecture and design for complex enterprise environments

• Demonstrated expertise across security architecture and secure networking, cloud, identity (both on premises and cloud), endpoint, application security, data protection, and detection and response

• Proven ability to lead threat modeling and architecture reviews, and to make consequential technical decisions for high-value or high-availability systems

• Working knowledge of AI/ML architecture and security, including secure MLOps, model and data governance, generative AI, RAG, AI agents, prompt injection, model supply-chain risk, sensitive-data exposure, access controls, and monitoring

• Ability to translate complex technical risk into clear recommendations for engineering teams, business stakeholders, and executive leaders

• Strong cross-functional leadership, facilitation, written communication, and mentoring skills, with a record of influencing decisions without direct authority

Preferred:

• Advanced experience with vulnerability assessment, security risk analysis, and risk-based prioritization

• Expertise in application security, secure software development, and the OWASP Top 10 and OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications

• Experience designing security for public cloud, hybrid environments, infrastructure as code, and CI/CD pipelines

• Familiarity with frameworks such as NIST CSF, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATT&CK, or MITRE ATLAS

• Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, SABSA, or equivalent

This position is based in our Reston, VA office and offers a hybrid work schedule.

The pay range is $164,300 - $222,300.

The anticipated annual base salary range for this position is noted above, however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience. jobs.description:
Legend Biotech is a global biotechnology company dedicated to treating and, one day, curing life-threatening diseases. Headquartered in Bridgewater, New Jersey, we are advancing the next generation of cell therapy through a portfolio of innovative technologies, including autologous, allogeneic, and in vivo cell therapy approaches. Our research spans chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T), T-cell receptor (TCR-T), natural killer (NK) cell-based therapies, and other emerging platforms designed to transform the treatment of serious diseases. From our global network of research and development sites, we are committed to discovering and developing safe, effective, and cutting-edge therapies for patients worldwide.

Legend Biotech entered into a global collaboration agreement with Johnson & Johnson to jointly develop and commercialize CARVYKTI® (ciltacabtagene autoleucel; cilta-cel). Through this strategic partnership, we combine complementary expertise and capabilities to advance innovative immunotherapies for patients living with multiple myeloma.

Legend Biotech is seeking an Associate Director, Regulatory Affairs as part of the Regulatory Affairs team based in Somerset, NJ.

Role Overview

The Associate Director of Regulatory Affairs is responsible for independently developing, coordinating and executing the global regulatory strategies. The Associate Director will represent Regulatory Affairs on global cross-functional teams and provide oversight on regulatory strategy implementation for the assets. The Associate Director will interact with health authorities to seek feedback and reach alignment on regulatory strategies; oversee activities for regulatory filings and ensure timely and high-quality submissions. The Associate Director will also work closely with collaboration partner on a key asset.

• Responsible to independently develop innovative, robust global regulatory strategies and ensure their efficient and effective execution for Legend pipeline programs.

• Interface with the FDA and other health authorities to seek feedback and alignment on pre-clinical and clinical development strategies.

• Represent Legend regulatory affairs in external collaborations.

• Serve as the regulatory affairs reviewer in the promotional material review committee.

• Coach and mentor junior members in their roles on global project teams.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

• Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

• What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

• It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS*

*Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

True Anomaly is seeking an MBSE Engineer in support of space and missile defense programs. This individual will serve as a technical SME for Cameo-based MBSE model development and SysML best practices, contributing tothe development of digital thread architecture and ecosystem operation. This role is responsible for developing, maintaining, and governing system models across complex space and missile defense programs, while also assisting with digital thread architecture development and being involved in systems engineering processes in alignment with Department of Defense (DoD)/Department of War (DoW) policies and industry standards. This includes developing and managing models created organically, working with subcontractors and evaluating their work, and integrating models provided externally from partners and the U.S. Government. This position will report to the Digital Thread Architect/Director of Digital Engineering.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Serve as a Cameo MBSE SME, providing technical leadership, mentoring, and governance for SysML-based system models

• Develop, maintain, and integrate MBSE artifacts supporting space systems, spacecraft, satellites, and missile defense weapon systems

• Work closely with the Systems Engineering team in capturing the full-spectrum of activities using model-based approaches, including: Requirements analysis and traceability Functional and logical architecture development Interface definition and system decomposition Verification and validation modeling

• Support System of Systems Engineering activities and model integration

• Apply and tailor MBSE practices in accordance with DoDI 5000.97, DoDI 5000.88, DoD Digital Engineering and Systems Engineering guidance documents, industry standards, recommended practices, and internal engineering requirements

• Utilize the Cameo platform to create and manage a model-based, authoritative representation of system requirements, architecture, behavior, interfaces, and verification to enable traceability, trade studies, business and technical decisions, and lifecycle decision-making for complex systems.

• Assist in integrating MBSE models with enterprise PLM tools, including Teamcenter, Jama, NX CAD, and other data systems, to enable lifecycle data continuity

jobs.title: Strategic Partnerships & Ops Lead, Physical AI
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Sieve is a multimodal lab curating the world’s highest-quality training datasets, spanning video, audio, images, text, and 3D. We combine exabyte-scale data infrastructure with novel multimodal understanding techniques to push the frontier of foundation models. We exist to solve one of the biggest bottlenecks in AI: high-quality training data.

We partner with top AI labs and did $XXM last quarter alone, with a team of roughly 40 people. We raised our Series A from firms including Matrix Partners, Swift Ventures, Y Combinator, and AI Grant.




WHY NOW

Physical AI needs data from real industrial environments — factories, manufacturing lines, and operations that don’t show up on the open web. Unlocking that access, and running the ops that turn it into lab-grade data, is a core growth constraint. You’ll join early enough to build both the partnerships and the operating system behind them.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This role mixes industrial partnerships with hands-on data ops. You’ll open doors into factories and similar environments, then run the workforce, QA, and platform work that turns that access into reliable multimodal data for frontier labs.

Strong fits look like industrials consultants, robotics operators, PE ops folks, or early ops hires who’ve already managed human-in-the-loop work and know how to earn trust with plant leaders and ops teams.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Open industrial access: Identify, pitch, and close partnerships with factories, manufacturers, and industrial operators; navigate security and compliance from first intro through live collection.

 - Operate the data ops platform: Run workforce management, task assignment, and QA workflows; build SOPs and training so quality stays at the bar frontier labs require.

 - Grow supply and partnerships: Source, onboard, and manage a distributed workforce for annotation, curation, and review; test acquisition and sourcing channels that scale.

 - Own product ops with engineering: Ship tooling improvements, track operational metrics, and close gaps in the data platform.

 - Turn one-offs into systems: Document playbooks so partner wins and ops workflows repeat across sites and programs.


REQUIREMENTS

 - Direct relationships into factories, manufacturing, or adjacent industrial environments — or a clear track record of building them

 - Mixed technical and non-technical skillset; comfortable with data tooling, light scripting, and spreadsheet-level analysis

 - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail; able to manage multiple concurrent work streams

 - Growth mindset: experience running or contributing to user acquisition, sourcing campaigns, or platform growth

 - Comfort with ambiguous, relationship-heavy work and the unglamorous ops needed to make a partnership live

 - Bachelor’s in CS, STEM, or equivalent practical experience; in-person at our SF HQ


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience managing human-in-the-loop data operations or annotation pipelines

 - At least 1 year of engineering experience or strong technical fluency

 - Prior work inside manufacturing, robotics deployment, factory ops, PE portfolio ops, or as an early hire / AI-lab ops lead

 - Familiarity with data quality frameworks, ML data pipelines, or physical AI


BENEFITS

 - 401(k) and full health insurance

 - Breakfast, lunch, and dinner covered, plus your choice of snacks

 - Ubers covered home



*All roles at Sieve require you to be onsite in San Francisco 5 days per week

jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Spacecraft Embedded Software Engineer on the Flight Software team is responsible for determining how our spacecraft behaves & operates in orbit and building reliable software to ensure it happens. They are responsible for all phases of development, starting from requirements capture through testing and flight operational support.

Responsibilities

• Develop reliable firmware to control how the spacecraft, satellite bus, and reentry capsule operate through the entire mission.

• Own all aspects of software development, from design, testing, and integration.

• Scope projects including requirements capture and initial design trades given open-ended problems.

• Write quality structured bare metal, RTOS, or Linux based software for embedded processors in C++.

• Build highly reliable and available software systems.

• Ensure system quality and performance through software test, verification, and validation (V&V) techniques.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in computer science, math, physics, engineering or equivalent technical experience in safety critical software.

• 5+ years of experience in the development of spacecraft or similar safety critical software.

• Experience developing and testing real-time embedded hardware / software systems.

• Experience with development in C++, along with a strong understanding of language concepts.

Preferred Skills and Experience

jobs.title: Principal Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Our mission at HubSpot is to help millions of organizations grow better. As Principal, Marketing Measurement, you'll lead the evolution of how HubSpot measures and optimizes its marketing measurement and investments — building the measurement infrastructure and decision-making framework that enables confident capital allocation decisions across organic, paid, owned, and earned channels.

HubSpot operates a significant and growing marketing presence across organic channels, paid media, a robust content and media network, and earned and owned activations. As we scale through brand-led, multi-channel demand creation, we're building the capability to understand what drives incremental growth across all marketing levers and translate those insights into smarter investment decisions. This role leads that work, working closely with cross functional teams across Marketing, Finance, Data Science, Engineering, and Product — combining marketing mix modeling, incrementality testing, multi-touch and modernized attribution, and predictive forecasting into a unified measurement capability that serves Marketing and Finance alike.

This is a high-visibility role for someone who combines deep measurement expertise with the strategic instincts to connect analytical rigor to the decisions that matter most.

What You'll Do

Measurement Strategy & Attribution

• Deep understanding of full funnel Marketing strategy and techniques.

• Own and evolve the marketing measurement framework across organic, paid, owned, Brand, LLM/AEO, media/creators, and earned channels — establishing a single, consistent view of how marketing investment drives revenue.

• Own and develop how marketing tracks full funnel attribution across the buyer journey across all channels and touchpoints.

• Modernize attribution methodology — moving beyond last-click toward view-based, multi-touch, and buying-group-aware models that capture the full influence of marketing activity on the path to revenue.

• Develop executive-ready reporting and performance narratives that connect marketing investment to revenue outcomes, enabling capital allocation decisions with confidence.

Marketing Mix Modeling & Incrementality

• Build and operate Marketing Mix Models that quantify the marginal ROI of investment across channels — enabling evidence-based scenario planning and capital allocation between paid, owned, and earned.

• Establish and scale an incrementality testing program — designing holdout methodology, running causal experiments, and translating results into investment recommendations.

• Partner with Marketing and Finance leadership to move budget conversations from channel-by-channel negotiation toward joint, evidence-based investment planning.

Predictive Analytics & Forecasting

• Build and operationalize predictive LTV models that connect upstream marketing signals to downstream revenue outcomes — enabling spend decisions grounded in expected long-term customer value.

• Develop multi-horizon revenue forecasting capabilities that translate real-time marketing indicators into expected ARR outcomes, giving Marketing and Finance a continuously updated view of performance.

• Drive the build vs. buy roadmap for predictive tooling — evaluating vendor solutions, managing external partnerships, and defining where proprietary models create lasting advantage.

Data Science Leadership

• Lead and direct data science execution toward measurement priorities — maintaining the technical depth to design experiments, validate methodology, and hold quality bar on outputs.

• Advance AI and machine learning applications across measurement, attribution, targeting, and forecasting to improve the speed and accuracy of marketing decision-making.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

• 10+ years in marketing analytics or marketing data science.

• Deep understanding of Marketing strategy and how it’s developed and executed on to inform and build build the right measurement approach behind it.

• Deep expertise in Marketing Mix Modeling and incrementality testing — hands-on experience building or operationalizing these capabilities and connecting outputs to capital allocation decisions.

• Experience building predictive LTV models and multi-horizon revenue forecasting — connecting leading marketing indicators to expected downstream revenue outcomes.

• Experience building or implementing multi-touch attribution models to measure impact across a B2B SaaS buyer’s journey.

• Track record of building a trusted Finance partnership — developing shared measurement frameworks that drive budget decisions, not just reporting.

• Strong technical fluency — able to design experiments, validate data science outputs, and direct execution teams effectively.

• Experience with modern, multi-touch attribution approaches across paid, owned, and earned channels, including view-based and buying-group-level measurement.

• Excellent executive communication skills — able to translate complex causal findings into clear investment recommendations for non-technical stakeholders.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

• Marketing measurement and leadership experience at a B2B SaaS or high-growth technology company.

• Data science background

• Experience with Brand and LLM/AEO/GEO measurement techniques and attribution.

• Background in or close partnership with paid media strategy and bidding optimization.

• Experience evaluating and managing external measurement vendors — MMM platforms, incrementality tools, or LTV providers.

• Familiarity with B2B buying-group measurement across complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles.

Key Qualities We'll Test For

• Measurement depth and methodology rigor

• Finance partnership and decision-making impact

• Predictive analytics and forecasting capability

• Strategic operating model and build vs. buy judgment

• Technical fluency and data science collaboration

• Executive communication and strategic storytelling

Pay & Benefits

The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

This resource will help guide how we recommend thinking about the range you see. Learn more about HubSpot’s compensation philosophy.

Benefits are also an important piece of your total compensation package. Explore the benefits and perks HubSpot offers to help employees grow better.

At HubSpot, fair compensation practices aren’t just about checking off the box for legal compliance. It’s about living out our value of transparency with our employees, candidates, and community.

Annual Cash Compensation Range:

$152,200—$243,500 USD

At HubSpot, we value both flexibility and connection. Whether you’re a Remote employee or work from the Office, we want you to start your journey here by building strong connections with your team and peers. If you are joining our Engineering team, you will be required to attend a regional HubSpot office for in-person onboarding. If you join our broader Product team, you’ll also attend other in-person events, such as your Product Group Summit and other gatherings, to continue building on those connections.

If you require an accommodation due to travel limitations or other reasons, please inform your recruiter during the hiring process. We are committed to supporting candidates who may need alternative arrangements

About HubSpot

HubSpot (NYSE: HUBS) is an AI-powered customer platform with all the software, integrations, and resources customers need to connect marketing, sales, and service. HubSpot's connected platform enables businesses to grow faster by focusing on what matters most: customers.

At HubSpot, bold is our baseline. Our employees around the globe move fast, stay customer-obsessed, and win together. Our culture is grounded in four commitments: Solve for the Customer, Be Bold, Learn Fast, Align, Adapt & Go!, and Deliver with HEART. These commitments shape how we work, lead, and grow.

We’re building a company where people can do their best work. We focus on brilliant work, not badge swipes. By combining clarity, ownership, and trust, we create space for big thinking and meaningful progress. And we know that when our employees grow, our customers do too.

Recognized globally for our award-winning culture by Comparably, Glassdoor, Fortune, and more, HubSpot is headquartered in Cambridge, MA, with employees and offices around the world.
